definition_zh: （线、发、绳的）一股；一缕；（绳缆的）股；（故事、论证的）线索；组成部分；（政策、计划的）组成部分；海滨；湖岸；使陷入困境；使搁浅
definition_en: one thin length of thread, hair or rope, or one connected line of a story or plan, or the shore of the sea
core_image: 双手把一大团毛线一点点分细，直到只剩下一根细线仍握在指间
scene: 雪夜里，一辆长途客车陷在公路旁，车门冻住，乘客只能看着车灯在风雪里明灭。A blizzard stranded dozens of passengers in a coach with no heating.
sceneCN: 这里 strand 表示「使被困住」（第 6 个义项：像船被搁浅一样与人失去联系）；句意：一场暴风雪害得几十名乘客被困在没有暖气的长途车里。画面里能看见的是雪夜、熄火的车灯，以及无处可去的乘客。

pos.zh: 名词：一股；一缕；绳缆的股；（故事、论证的）线索；（政策的）组成部分；海滨；湖岸
动词：使陷入困境；使搁浅

derivatives.zh: 由动词过去分词固化为形容词，义为「被困住的」「搁浅的」，如 stranded travellers。
地理学术语「滨线、沿岸线」，由海滨义项加上 line 构成。

senses.title: A single long thin piece
senses.definition: a single thin length of thread, hair, rope or wire viewed on its own
senses.definitionCN: 把线、头发、绳或铁丝单独分开来看的一根细长条
senses.example: One strand of her hair had come loose in the wind.
senses.exampleCN: 她有一缕头发被风吹散了。
senses.why: The Old English noun first named the shore or border, and English keeps the picture of a long narrow line, so one fibre taken apart is one strand.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词最早指海岸或边缘，英语保留了「细长的线条」这一画面，于是从整团里分出来的一根纤维也就是一个 strand。

senses.title: Threads twisted into cable
senses.definition: one of the separate lengths of fibre or wire that are twisted together to make a rope or cable
senses.definitionCN: 若干纤维或金属丝绞合成绳、缆时，其中各自独立的一股
senses.example: A steel cable of six strands snapped under the load.
senses.exampleCN: 一条六股的钢缆在重压下绷断了。
senses.why: When many thin lines are braided together, each line keeps its own identity inside the whole, and that is exactly what a strand is.
senses.whyCN: 许多细线编在一起时，每一根在整体里仍保留自己的身份，这正是 strand 所指的那种「股」。

senses.title: A thread of a story
senses.definition: one of the connected lines of thought, plot or argument that make up something larger
senses.definitionCN: 构成较大整体的若干相互关联的思路、情节或论点之一
senses.example: The identity of the narrator is a strand running through the novel.
senses.exampleCN: 叙述者的身份是贯穿整部小说的一条线索。
senses.why: A web of ideas is imagined as many threads woven together, so one line of a plot or argument is a strand too.
senses.whyCN: 人们把观念之网想象成许多线交织而成，所以情节或论证中的一条线也是一个 strand。

senses.title: A part of a plan
senses.definition: one part of a policy, plan or course of action that is combined with other parts
senses.definitionCN: 政策、计划或行动方案中与其他部分并行结合的一个部分
senses.example: Job training is only one strand of the new recovery policy.
senses.exampleCN: 职业培训只是新复苏政策的一个组成部分。
senses.why: The metaphor of woven threads turns into modern talk about the separate parts of a programme, each pulling in its own direction.
senses.whyCN: 「线交织」的比喻进入现代说法，用来指方案中各自发力、又共同成形的各个部分。

senses.title: The shore of a sea
senses.titleCN: 海滨；湖岸（书面上多用复数）
senses.definition: the land along the edge of a sea, lake or river, a literary word that is usually plural
senses.definitionCN: 海、湖或河边的陆地，属文学用语，通常以复数形式出现
senses.example: The ship broke up on a lonely strand on the northern coast.
senses.exampleCN: 那艘船在北部海岸一段荒凉的海滩上解体了。
senses.why: This is the plainest and oldest sense, for the Old English word simply meant the edge of the land by water.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素也最古老的义项，因为古英语原词本身就指陆地临水的边缘。

senses.title: To leave helpless on the shore
senses.definition: to leave a person or a vehicle helpless and stuck, the way a boat is left dry on the shore
senses.definitionCN: 使人或交通工具无助地被困住，就像船被留在岸上搁浅
senses.example: Falling snow stranded hundreds of drivers on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 大雪让数百名司机被困在高速公路上。
senses.why: The verb begins with ships driven onto the shore, and it widens into any person cut off from help, a line of descent that runs from shore to boat to helplessness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词作动词时从船只被冲上浅滩开始，逐渐扩展到任何一个与外界断绝援助的人，词义沿「岸—船—无助」这条线移动。

intro.en: Strand comes from Old English strand, the shore, a word shared with other Germanic languages and pushed toward the idea of a single thread by Dutch and Norse seafaring usage.
intro.cn: strand 来自古英语 strand（海岸），与其他日耳曼语同源；而「一股线」的意义，一般认为与荷兰语、北欧语中海员用绳的说法有关。

items.en: A reconstructed form, often written stranth, carries the sense of a border or edge.
items.cn: 一种重构形式（常写作 stranth）承载「边缘、边界」之义，属重构而非见诸文献的词形。

items.en: Strand plainly means the shore or bank of the sea.
items.cn: 古英语 strand 直言「海之岸边、岸滩」。

items.en: The old spelling stround appears beside strand, and strand wins.
items.cn: 中古英语兼用 stround 与 strand，最后 strand 胜出。

items.en: Seamen bring the sense of one of the twisted lengths that make a rope.
items.cn: 一般认为经由荷兰语与北欧语的海员用语，「绞成一股的绳条」义进入英语，年代说法略有出入。

items.en: The file sense of a connected line of story or argument grows out of the thread image.
items.cn: 由「线」的意象长出「情节线索、论证脉络」的含义，见诸十七至十九世纪的文本。

items.en: Policy talk and the verb meaning stranded turn it into an everyday word.
items.cn: 政策语境与动词「使被困」的广泛使用，使它成了日常词。

note.en: Strand the shore is the root; strand the thread is a sailor sense that later grew into metaphor.
note.cn: 「海岸」义的 strand 是根，而「一股线」义的 strand 来自海员用语，后来才长成比喻义。

entries.definition: a thin cord used for tying things
entries.definitionCN: 细绳。与 strand 拼写相近、义场相邻，但词源不同，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: a small river or a steady flow
entries.definitionCN: 小溪；水流。只是拼写相近，词源不同（一为水流，一为岸与绳）。

entries.definition: an area of sand or stones beside the sea
entries.definitionCN: 海滩；沙滩。与 strand 的「海滨」义同义，但是常用词，无「一股」义。

entries.definition: a single thin thread of material
entries.definitionCN: 纤维；一组中单根细丝。与「一股」义最近。

entries.definition: a thin line of spun cotton used in sewing, or a connecting line of a story
entries.definitionCN: 线；线索。同样从实物线延伸到故事线索。

entries.definition: to leave someone trapped with no way out
entries.definitionCN: 使困于孤处、孤立无援。与动词 strand 近义，语气更强。

normalIntro.en: Strand joins two pictures: the edge of land by water and a single twisted line, and from both the word grows.
normalIntro.cn: strand 连着两幅画面：水边的陆地边缘，和一根绞好的细线；两个意象各自长出了一串义项。

normal.en: A strand is what is left when you pull one thread from a rope.
normal.cn: 从绳子里抽出一根，那一根就是 strand。

normal.en: Cables are described by their strands, so a six strand cable has six lengths twisted together.
normal.cn: 钢缆按股描述，六股钢缆就是六根绞在一起。

normal.en: A plot has strands, just as a rope has strands, and each runs its own way.
normal.cn: 故事情节有 strands，正如绳子有股，每股各走各的方向。

normal.en: On the strand means on the shore, the oldest sense of the word.
normal.cn: on the strand 指在海滨，这是这个词最古老的用法。

normal.en: To be stranded is to be left on the shore like a boat the tide has dropped.
normal.cn: be stranded 就是像退潮后被留在岸上的船一样被困住。

abstract.en: See one hair lifted from a brush and held against the light.
abstract.cn: 想象从梳子上拈起一根头发，举到光里细看。

abstract.en: Watch six wires twist into one cable, then follow one wire with your eye.
abstract.cn: 想象六根钢丝绞成一条缆，再用眼睛盯住其中一根。

abstract.en: Picture a thin bright line running across the pages of a novel.
abstract.cn: 想象一条细细的亮线铺展在小说的每一页上。

examples.en: She twisted several strands of wool into a strong cord.
examples.cn: 她把几股羊毛捻成一根结实的绳。

examples.en: Teachers must follow each strand of the new curriculum.
examples.cn: 教师必须遵循新课程的每一条脉络。

examples.en: Heavy snow stranded thousands of commuters all night.
examples.cn: 大雪让数千名通勤者被困了整夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死攥的」——一只手死死攥着一根线，攥到它成了一股；这是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 strand（海岸、边缘）→ 中古英语 stround 与 strand 并用 → 一般认为经荷兰语、北欧语海员用绳的说法获得「一股绳、一缕」义 → 现代英语义项扩展为「线索、组成部分」与动词「使被困」。

sensesIntro.en: Strand starts at a single thin line, widens to the parts of a rope and of an argument, and returns to its oldest home, the edge of the sea, before the verb traps people there.
sensesIntro.cn: strand 从「一根细线」开始，扩展到绳子与论证中的「股、线索」，又回到它最古老的家，即海边，最后动词把人们困在那里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one thin twisted line, the shore of the sea, and the doing of leaving someone where they cannot get away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绞细的线、水边的岸，以及把人留在走不了的地方。

branches.en: A single fibre is the thread sense in its plainest form.
branches.cn: 一根纤维是最朴素的「线」义。

branches.en: Twisted lengths keep the picture of many threads in one whole.
branches.cn: 绞合的多股保留「多根线成一体」的画面。

branches.en: Lines of a story borrow the thread image.
branches.cn: 故事中的线索借用了「线」的意象。

branches.en: A policy strand is a thread inside a programme.
branches.cn: 政策的组成部分是方案内部的一条线。

branches.en: The shore is the root sense, and the verb puts people where a boat would be left.
branches.cn: 「海滨」是根义，动词则把人置于船被遗弃的那种处境。

intro.en: Strand has almost no affix life of its own; it grows through compounds and through the past participle stranded.
intro.cn: strand 本身几乎不靠词缀发展，而是通过复合词与过去分词 stranded 扩展。

latinIntro.en: No Latin source is recorded for strand, so only its English family is gathered here.
latinIntro.cn: strand 没有可考的拉丁语来源，所以这里只收它的英语词族。

items.example: The old word named the edge of the land by water.
items.exampleCN: 这个古词指陆地临水的边缘。

items.example: A seafaring sense wins a new meaning.
items.exampleCN: 海员用语给它添了新义。

items.example: The plural serves both noun meanings.
items.exampleCN: 复数形式对两个名词义项都适用。

items.example: Stranding comes from ships left on the shore.
items.exampleCN: 动名词形式表示「使被困」这一行为，源于搁浅的船。

items.meaning: forms the past participle and adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成过去分词与形容词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed gives stranded.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 stranded。

items.example: Stranded describes people cut off from help.
items.exampleCN: stranded 描述与援助隔绝的人。

items.example: The prefix multi- builds multistrand in technical writing.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 multi- 在技术文本中构成 multistrand。

items.example: Multistrand is used of wire and cable.
items.exampleCN: multistrand 用于描述多股钢丝与电缆。

items.example: The compound keeps the oldest noun sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词保留了最老的名词义。

definition_zh: 战略家；谋略家；（政治上的）策略家、智囊；善于长远谋划的人
definition_en: a person skilled in planning and directing long campaigns, especially in war, politics or business
core_image: 营帐里一位不穿甲的人，在沙盘上把棋子一颗颗推到位，再抬头看远处的山
scene: 选举前夜，竞选团队围坐一桌盯着一张航拍地图，只有策划者仍在重新排定最后一场演讲的地点。The strategist moved the final rally to a small town with a large undecided vote.
sceneCN: 这里 strategist 表示「竞选策略师」（第 2 个义项：政治场上的谋划者）；句意：策略师把最后一场集会挪到了一座尚未决定选票众多的小镇。画面里能看见的是选举前夜的航拍地图、坐着不动的团队成员，以及一个决定地点的人。

pos.zh: 名词：战略家；谋略家；策略家；智囊

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 strategia（统帅之职）来的基础名词，义为「战略；策略」；strategist 是其人格化派生。
加后缀 -ic 的形容词，义为「战略的；有战略意义的」。
加后缀 -ize 的动词，义为「制定策略」。
在 strategic 上加 -ally 的副词，义为「出于战略考虑地」。

senses.title: A planner of long campaigns
senses.definition: a person who is skilled in planning and directing a long and difficult campaign
senses.definitionCN: 擅长制定并指挥长期而艰难的行动的人
senses.example: The general was a patient strategist who thought years ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 那位将军是一位有耐心的战略家，凡事提前数年谋划。
senses.why: The Greek noun strategos named the general who led the army, and the one who plans rather than fights became the key member.
senses.whyCN: 古希腊语 strategos 指统帅军队的将军，而负责谋划而非亲自厮杀的人，成了其中最关键的角色，strategist 就由此而来。

senses.title: An expert in politics
senses.definition: a person who plans the way to win in politics or business by shaping opinion and timing
senses.definitionCN: 靠塑造舆论、把握时机来在政治或商业竞争中取胜的人
senses.example: Her campaign strategist persuaded her to speak to small towns.
senses.exampleCN: 她的竞选策略师说服她去小城镇演讲。
senses.why: The battlefield moved from land to the voting booth, and the same skill of preparing the ground was carried over.
senses.whyCN: 战场从土地转移到了投票站，而「提前布局、铺好场地」的能力被原样搬了过来。

senses.title: A careful long term thinker
senses.titleCN: 善谋远虑的人（引申用法）
senses.definition: a person known for planning far ahead and choosing the moment with care in ordinary life
senses.definitionCN: 在日常生活中以看得远、选准时机著称的人
senses.example: Grandmother is a quiet strategist with her family money.
senses.exampleCN: 奶奶在家庭理财上是个不动声色的谋算高手。
senses.why: Once the noun meant planning, it stretched until any careful planner could be called one.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示「谋划」，它就被拉宽，任何细心的规划者都可以被称作 strategist。

intro.en: Strategist comes through French stratège from Greek strategos, the general, literally the leader of an army, with -ist added on the English model of expert names.
intro.cn: strategist 经法语 stratège 来自希腊语 strategos（将军，字面意思是统率军队的人），后缀 -ist 是在英语中按「某方面专家」的构词习惯加上去的。

items.en: Strategos joins stratos, an encamped army, with agein, to lead.
items.cn: strategos 由 stratos（扎营的军队）与 agein（引导、率领）合成。

items.en: In Athens, strategos named the elected commander sent to lead the forces.
items.cn: 在雅典，strategos 指被选出来统率军队的指挥官。

items.en: Strategus is used for a military commander.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 strategus 用于指军事指挥官。

items.en: Stratège carries the Greek word toward modern European languages.
items.cn: 一般认为法语 stratège 把希腊词形带进了近代欧洲各语言。

items.en: English strategist makes the planner of wars a named kind of expert.
items.cn: 英语 strategist 在十八、十九世纪用于称呼专门谋划战争的人，催生了「战略家」这一类称号。

note.en: Strategist is the person noun of strategy; it names the mind behind the plan rather than the plan itself.
note.cn: strategist 是 strategy 的人格化名词，它指的是计划背后的头脑，而不是计划本身。

entries.definition: a plan for achieving a goal
entries.definitionCN: 战略；策略。词形与 strategist 几乎同根，只是去掉 -ist。

entries.definition: relating to strategy
entries.definitionCN: 战略的；有战略意义的。strategist 的形容词同族。

entries.definition: a clever trick used to gain an advantage
entries.definitionCN: 计谋；诡计。拼写与发音相近，本是希腊语中与军阵同说的一脉，但表达的是计谋而非人。

entries.definition: a person skilled in the details of an immediate move
entries.definitionCN: 战术家；擅长眼前具体行动的人。与战略家相对。

entries.definition: a person who plans a complicated operation
entries.definitionCN: 主谋；出谋划策者。多指策划复杂行动的人，偏口语。

entries.definition: a person who makes plans of any kind
entries.definitionCN: 规划者。范围更宽泛，不限于军事与政治。

normalIntro.en: Strategist holds strateg, the army camp of Greek strategos, plus ist, meaning the expert, so the word names the mind of the campaign.
normalIntro.cn: strategist 里有 strateg（希腊语 strategos 中的「军队营地」）加上 ist（表示专家的后缀），所以这个词指的是战役背后的那只脑袋。

normal.en: Attach ist to strategy and you get the one who does strategy.
normal.cn: strategy 加上 ist，就是做战略的那个人。

normal.en: Military strategists are remembered for the battles they avoided.
normal.cn: 军事战略家之所以出名，往往是因为他们避开的那些仗。

normal.en: A campaign strategist sells a message the way a shop sells goods.
normal.cn: 竞选策略师兜售信息，就像店铺兜售货物。

normal.en: Do not mix strategist with stratagem: one is a person, one is a trick.
normal.cn: 别把 strategist 与 stratagem 混了：前者是人，后者是计谋。

normal.en: Compare tactic and strategy: the tactician handles the step, the strategist handles the course.
normal.cn: 对比 tactic 与 strategy：战术家管走一步，战略家管整条路。

abstract.en: See a hand slide a tiny flag across a sand table and stop on a hill.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在沙盘上推着小旗滑过去，停在一座山丘前。

abstract.en: Imagine a map pinned to a wall, and one person quietly moving a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上钉着一张地图，一个人悄悄挪动一枚小磁石。

abstract.en: Picture a person who stays seated while everyone else rushes out.
abstract.cn: 想象所有人都往外冲时，有一个人仍坐着不动。

examples.en: A good strategist knows when to hold back and wait.
examples.cn: 好的战略家懂得何时按兵不动、等待时机。

examples.en: The party hired two strategists to reshape its message.
examples.cn: 该党聘请了两位策略师来重塑自己的信息。

examples.en: History remembers the strategists who won without fighting.
examples.cn: 历史记住的是那些不战而胜的谋略家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死抓特级」——凡事先抓住「特级」的关键处来谋划，像战略家先定要点；这是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 stratos（军队营阵）+ agein（统率）→ strategos（将军）→ 晚期拉丁 strategus → 法语 stratège → 英语 strategy 与 strategist（加 -ist 表人），核心义「统军与谋划的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Strategist begins as the general, then narrows into the planner of any long campaign, and finally loosens into any careful long term thinker.
sensesIntro.cn: strategist 起初就是将军，随后收窄为任何长期战役的谋划者，最后又放宽为任何善谋远虑的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seated planner moving markers across a map while others go out to act.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位坐着的人在地图上挪动标记，其他人则出去行动。

branches.en: The general as planner is the root sense.
branches.cn: 作为谋划者的将军是根义。

branches.en: The political strategist keeps the campaign frame and changes the field.
branches.cn: 政治策略师保留战役框架，只换了战场。

branches.en: The loose sense names any long term planner in daily life.
branches.cn: 宽泛义指日常生活中任何长远谋划者。

branches.en: Both kinds read public mood and choose the moment.
branches.cn: 两类人都读得懂人心向背，并挑选出手时机。

branches.en: In family and office as in politics, the quiet planner is the one who sets the agenda.
branches.cn: 无论在政治、家庭还是办公室，定议程的都是那个安静的谋划者。

intro.en: Strategist is strategy plus the person suffix ist, and the whole family rests on the Greek word for army and leading.
intro.cn: strategist 是 strategy 加上表人的后缀 ist，整个词族都建立在希腊语「军队、统率」上。

latinIntro.en: Latin took over the Greek military word as strategus, and -ista in Greek gave the modern person suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语以 strategus 接收了这个希腊军事词，而希腊语的 -ista 演变为现代的「表人」后缀。

items.example: Strategos is the source of strategy.
items.exampleCN: strategos 是 strategy 的来源。

items.example: Stratos is the source of the military half of this word.
items.exampleCN: 词根 stratos 也进入了英语地层类的词。

items.example: Agein supplies the leading half of the word.
items.exampleCN: agein 提供「率领」那一半含义。

items.meaning: a plan for a long campaign
items.example: Strategy is the plan, strategist is the planner.
items.exampleCN: strategy 是计划，strategist 是做计划的人。

items.example: The suffix -ist turns strategy into strategist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 把 strategy 变成 strategist。

items.example: Strategic marks the quality of the plan.
items.exampleCN: strategic 描述计划的性质。

items.example: Stratagem keeps the trick sense of the same field.
items.exampleCN: stratagem 保留了同一词场的「计谋」义。

items.example: A tactician works beside every strategist.
items.exampleCN: 每个战略家身边都有一位战术家。

definition_zh: 精力旺盛的；积极的；费力的；繁重的；剧烈的（运动）；坚决的；激昂的
definition_en: needing great effort or energy, or showing a great deal of energy and firmness
core_image: 一个人弓着上身、额头绷紧，把一件沉重的东西一步步往上推
scene: 清晨的山道陡得几乎没有台阶，登山的人肩上都捆着行李，每上一段都要停下来喘气。The climb was strenuous, and even fit walkers stopped every few minutes to rest.
sceneCN: 这里 strenuous 表示「费力的、繁重的」（第 2 个义项：需要极大体力的任务）；句意：这段攀爬十分费力，连体能好的人每走几分钟都得停下来歇一歇。画面里能看见的是陡坡、捆着行李的肩膀，以及不断停下喘气的人。

pos.zh: 形容词：精力旺盛的；积极的；费力的；繁重的；剧烈的；坚决的

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ously 的副词，义为「奋力地；坚决地」，如 strenuously object。
加后缀 -ness 的名词，义为「费力；干劲十足」。
固定搭配，义为「强烈反对」，体现「坚决」义这一分支。

senses.title: Very energetic and active
senses.definition: full of energy, eager and active in what one does
senses.definitionCN: 充满精力，做事积极而热情
senses.example: She led a strenuous campaign to save the old library.
senses.exampleCN: 她发起了一场干劲十足的保旧图书馆运动。
senses.why: The Latin stem meant brisk and eager, so the adjective first praises energy in a person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词干本义是「精神焕发、积极」，所以这个词最初是在夸一个人身上的干劲。

senses.title: Needing great effort
senses.definition: requiring great physical or mental effort and lasting a long time
senses.definitionCN: 需要大量体力或脑力，且持续时间较长
senses.example: Clearing the avalanche debris was strenuous work for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 清理雪崩残骸对全村来说是件费力的活。
senses.why: From praising the energy of a person the adjective slides onto the task that demands such energy.
senses.whyCN: 从称赞人身上的精力，这个词滑向了「需要这种精力」的任务本身。

senses.title: Demanding on the body
senses.definition: of exercise or activity, hard enough to raise the heart rate and strain the muscles
senses.definitionCN: 指运动或活动强度大，足以抬高心率、消耗肌肉
senses.example: Doctors told him to avoid strenuous exercise after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 医生嘱咐他术后避免剧烈运动。
senses.why: Medical use takes the effort sense and measures it: strenuous exercise is the kind the body really feels.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法接过「费力」义并给它定了量：strenuous exercise 就是身体真真切切承受得住的强度。

senses.title: Strongly held
senses.definition: of views, denials or objections, stated with force and firmness
senses.definitionCN: 指观点、否认或反对表达得有力而坚决
senses.example: The company issued a strenuous denial of the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 公司对这一传言予以坚决否认。
senses.why: The energy sense drifts from the body to the voice, and a strenuous protest is one pushed with full strength.
senses.whyCN: 干劲从身体转移到了声音里，strenuous 的抗议就是拼尽全力发出的抗议。

intro.en: Strenuous comes straight from Latin strenuus, brisk, energetic or active, with the ending changed on the model of adjectives in ous.
intro.cn: strenuous 直接来自拉丁语 strenuus（精神抖擞、有活力），词尾按英语中 ous 形容词的模式改写。

items.en: Strenuus describes a person who is brisk, lively and active.
items.cn: 拉丁语 strenuus 描述一个人精神抖擞、活跃而能干。

items.en: The adverb strenue is used of a runner moving with full speed.
items.cn: 副词 strenue 用于形容全速奔跑、发力的人。

items.en: The earlier root is uncertain; some relate it to a word for strength, but this is not established.
items.cn: 更早的词根来源不确定；有人把它同表示「力气」的词联系起来，但未成定论。

items.en: English takes the adjective and keeps the sense of energy first.
items.cn: 英语引入该形容词时，最初保留「有劲头」的含义。

items.en: The adjective moves from people to tasks, so strenuous work becomes hard work.
items.cn: 这一形容词从人转到了任务上，于是 strenuous work 成了辛苦的活。

note.en: Strenuous praises energy in people and effort in tasks; its family is small but firmly Latin.
note.cn: strenuous 既称赞人身上的干劲，也描述任务所需的努力；它的词族不大，但明显来自拉丁语。

entries.definition: with great effort or firmness
entries.definitionCN: 奋力地；坚决地。strenuous 直接加 -ly 的副词形式。

entries.definition: the quality of being strenuous
entries.definitionCN: 费力；干劲。由 strenuous 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: very strict or severe
entries.definitionCN: 严格的；紧缩的。只是拼写相近，词源不同（源自 squeezing 的意象）。

entries.definition: strong and full of energy
entries.definitionCN: 有力的；精力充沛的。与「精力旺盛」义最近。

entries.definition: needing great effort over a long time
entries.definitionCN: 艰巨的；费力的。与「费力」义最接近。

entries.definition: hard and demanding to do
entries.definitionCN: 艰难的；费劲的。口语中接近「费力」，但更随意。

normalIntro.en: Strenuous keeps the Latin idea of a body running at full speed, so it praises energy and also names the work that drains it.
normalIntro.cn: strenuous 保留了拉丁语里「身体全速发力」的想法，所以它既夸人的干劲，也指那种把干劲榨干的工作。

normal.en: Strenuous exercise is the kind that leaves you breathless.
normal.cn: strenuous exercise 就是那种让你喘不上气的运动。

normal.en: A strenuous effort is one made at full strength.
normal.cn: strenuous effort 就是拼尽全力做出的努力。

normal.en: Strenuous opposition is loud and firm, not quiet disapproval.
normal.cn: strenuous opposition 是响亮而坚决的反对，不是小声的不满。

normal.en: Strenuous and vigorous differ: one notes the demand, one praises the strength.
normal.cn: strenuous 与 vigorous 不同：前者说明负担，后者夸赞力气。

normal.en: Remember strenuous by its length: the long word is the long climb.
normal.cn: 用长度记 strenuous：这个词长，就像那段长坡。

abstract.en: See a person pushing a heavy cart up a slope, forehead tight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人弓着身子把重车往坡上推，额头的筋都绷着。

abstract.en: Feel your own breath shorten as you climb a long staircase.
abstract.cn: 想象自己爬一段长楼梯，呼吸一点点变短。

abstract.en: Picture a fist raised in a firm complaint, not lowered.
abstract.cn: 想象一个为坚持反对而举起的拳头，始终没有放下。

examples.en: The work was strenuous but the team never complained.
examples.cn: 这活儿很费力，但团队从没抱怨过。

examples.en: Patients should avoid strenuous activity for a week.
examples.cn: 病人一周内应避免剧烈活动。

examples.en: She made a strenuous objection to the plan.
examples.cn: 她对这个计划表示强烈反对。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死踹牛」——一个人咬牙死死踹着牛车往前推，一脚一脚都使出全力；这是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 strenuus（精神抖擞、活跃）→ 英语 strenuous（先指人有干劲，后指任务费力），更早的词根来源不确定，不宜强行与「力气」一词挂钩。

sensesIntro.en: Strenuous starts as energy in a person, then moves onto the work that demands it, narrows to exercise, and finally shifts from the body to the voice of protest.
sensesIntro.cn: strenuous 从人身上的干劲出发，转到需要这股干劲的任务，再收窄为运动强度，最后从身体移到了抗议的声音里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body leaning into a heavy thing, pushing it up while breathing hard.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体倾过去，顶着沉重的东西往上推，呼吸粗重。

branches.en: Energy in a person is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 人身上的干劲是最早的义项。

branches.en: The task that demands energy takes the adjective next.
branches.cn: 接下来这个形容词落到了需要干劲的任务上。

branches.en: Medical speech gives the effort a measured body limit.
branches.cn: 医学用语为这股费力划出了身体上的界限。

branches.en: The same effort becomes a voice raised in protest.
branches.cn: 同样的力气变成了一句高声的抗议。

branches.en: A strenuous denial is work: it takes sustained force to keep saying no.
branches.cn: 坚决的否认也是苦功：要持续用力才能一直说不。

intro.en: Strenuous is a Latin adjective plus English endings; the family is built with ous, ly and ness.
intro.cn: strenuous 是拉丁形容词加上英语词尾，词族主要靠 ous、ly、ness 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin strenuus means brisk and active; the adverb strenue shows the same energy.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 strenuus 意即「精神抖擞」，副词 strenue 表示同样的干劲。

items.example: Strenuus is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: strenuus 是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: Strenue describes someone moving with all speed.
items.exampleCN: strenue 描述全速前行的人。

items.example: The suffix -ous gives strenuous in English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 在英语中构成 strenuous。

items.example: Strenuously is common with deny and object.
items.exampleCN: strenuously 常与 deny、object 搭配。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns the adjective into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 把形容词变为副词。

items.example: Strenuousness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: strenuousness 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The suffix -ness builds the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成抽象名词。

items.example: Stringent looks similar but has a different root.
items.exampleCN: stringent 形似，但词根不同。

items.example: Vigorous is the closest everyday partner.
items.exampleCN: vigorous 是最近义的日常同伴。

definition_zh: 冲突；争斗；（家庭或团体内部的）不和、纷争
definition_en: angry disagreement or fighting between people, groups, or nations
core_image: 两股绳子被向两边猛拉，越绷越紧，直到纤维一根根断开
scene: 兄弟俩为了一间铺子吵了多年，邻居见了都绕着走。Years of strife between the two brothers left the whole family exhausted.
sceneCN: 这里 strife 是「冲突；争斗」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间激烈的争执与对抗）；句意：兄弟俩常年的纷争让整个家庭疲惫不堪。

pos.zh: 冲突；争斗；不和；纷争

derivatives.zh: 拼命努力；奋斗（与 strife 同出古法语 estrif，义为「争吵；较量」，努力义是后起的引申）
奋斗；努力（strive 加 -ing 构成，突出「绷紧去争取」的动作）

senses.title: Angry conflict between people
senses.definition: bitter disagreement or fighting between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间或群体之间激烈的分歧与争斗
senses.example: The village has known little peace since the strife began.
senses.exampleCN: 纷争开始以来，这个村庄很少安宁。
senses.why: The Old French estrif meant a quarrel, so the core image is two sides pulling hard against each other.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 estrif 本义为争吵，所以核心画面是双方用力互拉，谁也不肯松手。

senses.title: A state of social disorder
senses.definition: violent unrest or disorder inside a country or a community
senses.definitionCN: 国家或社群内部发生的暴力动荡与失序
senses.example: Civil strife forced many families to flee the capital.
senses.exampleCN: 内乱迫使许多家庭逃离首都。
senses.why: When the quarrel spreads from two people to a whole society, it becomes civil strife.
senses.whyCN: 当争吵从两个人扩散到整个社会，就成了内乱，这是第一义从个体层面放大到社会层面。

senses.title: Conflict within a family or group
senses.definition: disagreement that spoils the harmony of a family, team, or workplace
senses.definitionCN: 破坏家庭、团队或职场和睦的争执
senses.example: Constant domestic strife wore the young couple down.
senses.exampleCN: 不断升级的家庭不和拖垮了这对年轻夫妇。
senses.why: The same pulling-apart image works indoors, where it shows up as quarrels at the table and cold silences.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「互相拉扯」画面也发生在屋子里，表现为饭桌上的争吵和长时间的冷战。

senses.title: A struggle or bitter effort
senses.definition: a difficult struggle against hardship or opposition, often in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 与困苦或对立力量进行的艰难抗争，多用于文学语体
senses.example: The novel tells of a pioneer life of hardship and strife.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说讲述了拓荒生活中充满艰辛与抗争的日子。
senses.why: Strifes and strivings grew side by side, so strife can also point to the effort itself, not only to the fight.
senses.whyCN: strife 与表示努力的 strive 一直并肩使用，所以它也能指奋斗本身，而不只是争斗。

senses.title: A source of conflict
senses.definition: something that causes quarrelling, such as money or land
senses.definitionCN: 引起争吵的事物，如钱财、土地或继承权
senses.example: The old orchard was a constant apple of strife in the family.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老果园一直是这个家里争吵不断的话题。
senses.why: People can speak of strife as a thing rather than an event, meaning whatever makes the pulling start.
senses.whyCN: 人们也能把 strife 当作一件「东西」来说，指的是让拉扯开始的那个起因。

intro.en: Strife comes from Old French estrif, a quarrel, which probably goes back to a Germanic word for fighting.
intro.cn: strife 来自古法语 estrif（争吵），一般认为可上溯到日耳曼语中表示搏斗的词语。

items.en: A Germanic source is usually reconstructed, likely from a word meaning to strive or fight.
items.cn: 一般认为有日耳曼语来源，重构形式可能表示「努力、搏斗」，具体词形来源不确定。

items.en: Estrif means a quarrel, contest, or fighting.
items.cn: estrif 意为争吵、较量或搏斗。

items.en: Strif enters English in the thirteenth century with the sense of a quarrel.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，strif 于十三世纪进入英语，义为争吵。

items.en: The spelling strife settles in, and the verb strive grows beside it.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 strife，动词 strive 也在它旁边发展出来。

items.en: Writers use strife for civil war, religious conflict, and private quarrels alike.
items.cn: 早期现代英语中，strife 兼指内战、宗教冲突与私人争吵。

items.en: The noun stays slightly formal, often paired with civil, industrial, or sectarian.
items.cn: 现代英语里它略带正式色彩，常与表示内乱、劳资、教派的形容词搭配。

note.en: Strife is the noun of friction, close to strive, striven, and to words such as conflict, discord, and quarrel.
note.cn: strife 是表示「摩擦、拉扯」的名词，与 strive、striven 同族，与 conflict、discord、quarrel 等词义相近。

entries.definition: to try very hard
entries.definitionCN: 努力；奋斗；力争

entries.definition: the past participle of strive
entries.definitionCN: strive 的过去分词

entries.definition: loud and harsh
entries.definitionCN: 刺耳的；声嘶力竭的（只是以 stri- 开头，与 strife 词源无关）

entries.definition: a serious disagreement or fight
entries.definitionCN: 冲突；争执

entries.definition: lack of agreement between people
entries.definitionCN: 不和；意见分歧

entries.definition: an angry argument
entries.definitionCN: 争吵；口角

normalIntro.en: Strife is the noise of a quarrel: two sides pull, voices rise, nothing stays calm.
normalIntro.cn: strife 是争吵的声响：两边各拉一头，嗓门越来越大，谁都不肯冷静。

normal.en: Strife and strive share one root: quarrelling is two people straining against each other.
normal.cn: strife 与 strive 同根：争吵就是两个人朝相反方向使劲。

normal.en: Civil strife means fighting inside one country, not across borders.
normal.cn: civil strife 指一个国家内部的互相争斗，而非跨国战争。

normal.en: Industrial strife is the phrase for strikes and disputes between bosses and workers.
normal.cn: industrial strife 是形容老板与工人之间罢工与争执的固定说法。

normal.en: Remember sectarian strife: conflict between religious groups.
normal.cn: 记住 sectarian strife：不同宗教派别之间的冲突。

normal.en: Compare conflict: conflict is neutral and common, strife sounds older and more literary.
normal.cn: 对比 conflict：conflict 中性且常用，strife 听起来更古老、更文学化。

abstract.en: Picture two ropes tied together and pulled by opposite teams until the knot tears.
abstract.cn: 想象两条绳子系在一起，被两队人朝相反方向猛拉，直到绳结撕裂。

abstract.en: Imagine a quiet town where shop windows suddenly crack all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座安静的小镇，所有店铺的玻璃忽然同时碎裂。

abstract.en: Think of a single chair at a dinner table that everyone keeps arguing over.
abstract.cn: 想象餐桌旁只有一把椅子，人人都为它争个不停。

examples.en: Economic collapse often brings social strife in its wake.
examples.cn: 经济崩溃往往会随之带来社会冲突。

examples.en: Their marriage ended after years of silent strife.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻在多年无声的不和之后走到了尽头。

examples.en: The report warns that industrial strife could slow the recovery.
examples.cn: 报告警告说，劳资纠纷可能拖慢复苏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死拽夫」——夫妻二人各拽一头，谁也不松手，就是 strife；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 estrif（争吵）→ 中古英语 strif / strife；一般认为更早来自日耳曼语表示「搏斗、使劲」的词语（具体词形来源不确定）；同族动词 strive 表示「拼命努力」。

sensesIntro.en: Strife starts as a quarrel, widens into social unrest, enters the home, and then lends its pulling image to hard struggle and to the very cause of conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: strife 从一场争吵出发，扩大到社会动荡，再进入家庭内部，最后把「互相拉扯」的画面借给艰辛奋斗，也用来指引起纷争的原因。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two ropes pulled in opposite directions until they tear.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条绳子被反向拉扯，直到绷断。

branches.en: A quarrel between people is the plain sense.
branches.cn: 人与人之间的争吵是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: Crowding the quarrel on a national scale gives civil strife.
branches.cn: 把争吵放大到国家规模，就是内乱。

branches.en: Inside a family, strife is both the quarrel and whatever it is about.
branches.cn: 在家庭内部，strife 既指争吵本身，也指争吵所围绕的事物。

branches.en: The pulling image also serves as a name for hard struggle.
branches.cn: 「拉扯」的画面也用来称说艰辛的奋斗。

branches.en: Whether public or private, strife always breaks harmony apart.
branches.cn: 无论公共还是私人领域，strife 都意味着把和睦撕裂。

intro.en: Strife has no live English affix, but it shares a family with the verb strive and the noun striving.
intro.cn: strife 在现代英语里没有可拆的活前缀，它与动词 strive 和名词 striving 构成一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Strife is Germanic in ultimate origin, but it travelled through Old French estrif before reaching English.
latinIntro.cn: strife 的最终来源是日耳曼语，但它先进入古法语 estrif，再传入英语。

items.example: Estrif is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: estrif 是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: Strife keeps the Old French sense of a quarrel.
items.exampleCN: strife 保留了古法语「争吵」的含义。

items.example: The plural strifes is rare but recorded.
items.exampleCN: 复数 strifes 少见但确有记录。

items.example: Strive inherits the image of straining.
items.exampleCN: strive 继承了「使劲」的意象。

items.example: Striven is the older participle in use.
items.exampleCN: striven 是仍在使用的旧式分词。

items.example: Striving turns the verb into an activity.
items.exampleCN: striving 把动词变成一种活动。

items.example: Civil turns strife into a national conflict.
items.exampleCN: civil 让 strife 变成国家内部的冲突。

items.example: Strife-torn means ruined by long conflict.
items.exampleCN: strife-torn 表示被长期冲突摧残。

definition_zh: 严格的；严厉的；（规定、规则）苛刻的；（财政或条件）紧缩的
definition_en: very strict and demanding, or very tight and controlled
core_image: 一根绳子被收紧到几乎勒进皮肉，多一分力气就要勒破
scene: 实验室门口贴满清单，手套要换三次，记录本写错一个字就得重来。The lab has stringent rules about handling every sample.
sceneCN: 这里 stringent 是「严格的；（规定）苛刻的」（第 1 个义项：规则定得极严、要求毫不放松）；句意：这个实验室对处理每个样本都有严格的规矩。

pos.zh: 严格的；严厉的；苛刻的；紧缩的

derivatives.zh: stringent 加 -ency 构成，义为「严格；严苛；紧缩」
stringent 加 -ly 构成，义为「严格地；严厉地」
绳、线；用线串起来（与 stringent 同出拉丁语 stringere「拉紧」，但英语中另作独立词使用）

senses.title: Very strict and demanding
senses.definition: demanding that rules or standards be followed exactly
senses.definitionCN: 要求人们丝毫不差地遵守规定或标准的
senses.example: The airline has stringent checks before every flight.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司在每次飞行前都做严格的检查。
senses.why: Latin stringere means to draw tight, so a strict rule is one pulled so taut that nothing can slip through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 stringere 意为拉紧，所以严格的规定就像一根绷到极限的绳子，什么都漏不过去。

senses.title: Severe in treatment
senses.definition: harsh and punishing in the way people are treated or judged
senses.definitionCN: 在对待或评判他人时严厉、不留情面的
senses.example: Critics called the new penalties too stringent for first offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者认为，对初犯者来说新处罚过于严厉。
senses.why: When the tight rope presses on people rather than on rules, the sense shifts from strict to harsh.
senses.whyCN: 当绷紧的绳子压在人与规则上时，词义就从「严格」滑向「严厉、不近人情」。

senses.title: Tightly controlled in money
senses.definition: kept low and tightly controlled, as of a budget or lending
senses.definitionCN: 指预算或信贷保持低水平并被严格控制的
senses.example: The school operated under a stringent budget for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这所学校多年在紧缩的预算下运作。
senses.why: Economics borrows the rope image for money: a stringent budget is a purse tied shut.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了「绳子」的意象来形容钱：紧缩的预算就是一只被扎紧口子的钱袋。

senses.title: Sound convincing
senses.definition: strong enough to convince, as of an argument or a proof
senses.definitionCN: 指论证或证据严密得足以使人信服的
senses.example: The theory survived a string of stringent tests.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论经受住了一连串严苛的检验。
senses.why: A test that is pulled tight lets no weak claim pass, so stringent proof is proof that holds under strain.
senses.whyCN: 绷紧的检验容不下任何站不住的说法，因此「严密的证据」就是经得起拉扯的证据。

intro.en: Stringent comes from Latin stringere, to draw tight or bind, which also gives us strain, strict, and stringent in the medical sense of tightening.
intro.cn: stringent 来自拉丁语 stringere（拉紧、捆紧），它同时派生了 strain、strict，也衍生出医学上「收缩的」用法。

items.en: Stringere means to draw tight, bind, or touch lightly.
items.cn: stringere 意为拉紧、捆紧或轻触。

items.en: In medicine the participle stringens describes something that tightens the body.
items.cn: 在医学用法中，分词 stringens 描述使身体收紧的事物。

items.en: The English adjective enters late, still close to the idea of binding.
items.cn: 英语形容词出现较晚，起初仍接近「捆紧」之意。

items.en: Stringent becomes a common word for laws, rules, and conditions that are tight.
items.cn: 到了十八世纪，stringent 常用来形容严格、苛刻的法律、规定与条件。

items.en: Economics and science adopt it: stringent budgets, stringent tests.
items.cn: 经济学与科学领域采用它，出现紧缩预算、严苛检验等说法。

note.en: Stringent shares its tightening root with strict, strain, and constrict, and sits among strict, rigorous, and severe in meaning.
note.cn: stringent 与 strict、strain、constrict 同有「拉紧」的词根，在词义上与 strict、rigorous、severe 相邻。

entries.definition: demanding exact obedience
entries.definitionCN: 严格的；要求服从的

entries.definition: to pull tight or make an effort
entries.definitionCN: 拉紧；使劲；压力

entries.definition: the quality of being strict
entries.definitionCN: 严格；紧缩；严苛

entries.definition: careful and thorough to a demanding standard
entries.definitionCN: 严密的；严谨的

entries.definition: very serious or harsh
entries.definitionCN: 严厉的；严重的

entries.definition: not strict
entries.definitionCN: 宽容的；宽松的

normalIntro.en: Stringent wears its meaning on its root: the same tightening hand behind strict and strain.
normalIntro.cn: stringent 把词义写在词根上：它和 strict、strain 出自同一次「拉紧」。

normal.en: Strict and stringent come from the same rope: what is strict follows rules, what is stringent is pulled even tighter.
normal.cn: strict 与 stringent 出同一条绳子：strict 指守规矩，stringent 则拉得更紧。

normal.en: The noun stringency means strictness in a formal tone.
normal.cn: 名词 stringency 以正式语气表示「严格、严苛」。

normal.en: Use stringent with rules, standards, measures, and budgets.
normal.cn: stringent 常与 rules、standards、measures、budgets 这些词搭配。

normal.en: Think of a string pulled tight: that is why it can also mean a very tight budget.
normal.cn: 想象一根被拉紧的绳子，这就是它也能表示「预算吃紧」的原因。

normal.en: Compare rigorous: rigorous stresses careful accuracy, stringent stresses severity.
normal.cn: 对比 rigorous：rigorous 强调细致精确，stringent 强调严厉苛刻。

abstract.en: Picture a metal band screwed down until the joints creak.
abstract.cn: 想象一条金属箍被越拧越紧，直到接缝嘎吱作响。

abstract.en: Imagine a doorman who checks every name twice and still asks again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门卫把每个名字核对两遍，还要再问一次。

abstract.en: Think of a wallet closed with a strap so tight that no coin slips out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个用皮带扎得极紧的钱包，一枚硬币也掉不出来。

examples.en: Stringent safety rules saved the plant from a serious accident.
examples.cn: 严格的安全规定使工厂免于一场严重事故。

examples.en: The city imposed stringent limits on car emissions.
examples.cn: 该市对汽车排放实施了严格的限制。

examples.en: Some argue that the sentence was stringently applied to the wrong person.
examples.cn: 有人认为这一判决被严厉地施加在了错误的人身上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死村真特」——村里规矩定得又严又苛刻，谁也不敢犯；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stringere（拉紧、捆紧）→ 分词 stringens → 英语 stringent；同根词有 strict、strain、constrict、restrict，核心义「绷紧、不留余地」。

sensesIntro.en: Stringent moves from a rule that is drawn tight, to harsh treatment, to money kept under tight control, and finally to proof strong enough to hold under strain.
sensesIntro.cn: stringent 从绷得极紧的规定，走到严厉的对待，再到被紧紧控制的钱财，最后落到经得起拉扯的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope drawn tight enough to cut the skin.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子收紧到几乎勒破皮肤。

branches.en: Rules drawn tight are the common sense today.
branches.cn: 绷紧的规矩是如今最常见的义项。

branches.en: Tightness applied to people becomes harshness.
branches.cn: 把「紧」施加到人身上，就成了严厉。

branches.en: Tightness applied to money becomes a stringent budget.
branches.cn: 把「紧」施加到钱财上，就成了紧缩的预算。

branches.en: Proof that survives the pull is called stringent.
branches.cn: 经得起拉扯的证据也被称作 stringent。

branches.en: Both the rule and its punishment share the same unyielding grip.
branches.cn: 规则与其惩罚共享同一种毫不松手的抓紧。

intro.en: Stringent is built on the Latin root string-, seen in strict and constrict, and takes the adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: stringent 建立在拉丁词根 string-（拉紧）之上，这一词根也见于 strict、constrict，并加形容词词尾 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin stringere, to draw tight, gives participle stringens and noun stringentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 stringere（拉紧）给出分词 stringens 与名词 stringentia。

items.example: Stringere is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: stringere 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Stringens gives the English adjective its shape.
items.exampleCN: stringens 给出英语形容词的形态来源。

items.example: The ending -ent turns a verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: Strict is the close cousin with the same root.
items.exampleCN: strict 是同根的近亲词。

items.example: Strain keeps the plain physical sense.
items.exampleCN: strain 保留了朴素的物理义。

items.example: The prefix con- plus strict gives constrict.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 con- 加 strict 构成 constrict。

items.example: The suffix -ency forms stringency.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ency 构成 stringency。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms stringently.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 stringently。

items.example: The word keeps the tightening metaphor.
items.exampleCN: 这个词保留了「拉紧」的隐喻。

definition_zh: 好学的；勤奋的；用功的；（对某事）特别留心的、刻意的
definition_en: spending much time on study, or showing careful effort and attention
core_image: 台灯下的人伏在桌上，书页一页页翻过去，笔记本记得密密麻麻
scene: 图书馆角落的灯几乎每晚最后熄灭，那个人总是书堆到下巴还嫌看不完。She was so studious that she had read every book on the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 studious 是「好学的；用功的」（第 1 个义项：把大量时间和心思都花在学习上）；句意：她如此好学，书架上每一本书都读过。

pos.zh: 好学的；勤奋的；用功的；留心的

derivatives.zh: studious 去 -ous 加 -ly 构成，义为「勤奋地；刻意地；小心翼翼地」
studious 加 -ness 构成，义为「好学；勤奋；用心」
工作室；录音室（与 studious 同出拉丁语 studium，但经意大利语转借，指「专心工作的地方」）

senses.title: Devoted to study
senses.definition: spending a lot of time reading and learning
senses.definitionCN: 花大量时间读书学习的
senses.example: He was a quiet, studious boy who rarely joined the games.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个安静用功的男孩，很少参加游戏。
senses.why: The Latin noun studium means eager pursuit, and studious keeps that picture of a person given over to books.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 studium 意为热切的追求，studious 保留了这种一心扑在书上的画面。

senses.title: Hardworking and diligent
senses.definition: putting steady effort into work of any kind
senses.definitionCN: 对任何工作都持续用力的
senses.example: Her studious habits made the small workshop famous.
senses.exampleCN: 她勤勉的习惯让这间小作坊出了名。
senses.why: The zeal behind study can be applied to any task, so studious also praises steady effort in general.
senses.whyCN: 藏在「学习」背后的那股热情可以用在任何事情上，所以 studious 也泛指踏踏实实的勤奋。

senses.title: Careful and deliberate
senses.definition: done with conscious care or effort, sometimes with a hint that it is unusual
senses.definitionCN: 有意用心用力去做，有时暗示这样做不太寻常或带点做作
senses.example: She gave the reporter a studious answer, avoiding names entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 她给了记者一个刻意斟酌过的回答，完全避开了姓名。
senses.why: A person who studies a thing watches it closely and on purpose, so a studious effort is an effort made with deliberate care.
senses.whyCN: 一个人仔细研究某物，就会刻意地盯着它看，因此「用心的努力」就带上了刻意与谨慎的色彩。

intro.en: Studious comes from Latin studiosus, eager or zealous, which grows from studium, a strong desire or pursuit of learning.
intro.cn: studious 来自拉丁语 studiosus（热切的、专心的），它源于 studium（强烈的愿望或对学问的追求）。

items.en: Studium means eagerness, zeal, or the pursuit of knowledge.
items.cn: studium 意为热望、热忱或对知识学问的追求。

items.en: Studiosus means eager, zealous, or devoted to study.
items.cn: studiosus 意为热切的、专心的或献身于钻研的。

items.en: Studieus carries the adjective into French with the sense of eager.
items.cn: studieus 把这一形容词带入法语，仍含「热切」之意。

items.en: The word enters English in the fourteenth century, meaning devoted to learning.
items.cn: 该词于十四世纪进入英语，义为专心向学。

items.en: Modern English extends the meaning to any careful, deliberate effort.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到任何小心而刻意的努力。

note.en: Studious is built from the Latin root studi-, seen in study and student, and it sits close to diligent, scholarly, and bookish in meaning.
note.cn: studious 由拉丁词根 studi- 构成，study 与 student 也出自这一词根；词义上与 diligent、scholarly、bookish 邻近。

entries.definition: to spend time learning
entries.definitionCN: 学习；研究

entries.definition: a person who is learning
entries.definitionCN: 学生

entries.definition: with careful and deliberate effort
entries.definitionCN: 勤奋地；刻意地

entries.definition: working hard and carefully
entries.definitionCN: 勤勉的；孜孜不倦的

entries.definition: showing serious academic knowledge
entries.definitionCN: 有学者风范的；学术性的

entries.definition: not working or studying
entries.definitionCN: 懒散的；闲散的

normalIntro.en: Studious carries study inside it: anyone who is studious is always studying.
normalIntro.cn: studious 的身体里就藏着 study：好学的人总在学习。

normal.en: Study plus -ous gives studious, full of study.
normal.cn: study 加上词尾 -ous 就是 studious，即「满脑子都是学习」。

normal.en: The adverb studiously means both diligently and deliberately.
normal.cn: 副词 studiously 既能表示勤奋地，也能表示刻意地。

normal.en: The noun studiousness names the habit of working hard.
normal.cn: 名词 studiousness 指勤奋好学的习惯。

normal.en: Studio shares the root: a place for devoted work.
normal.cn: studio 与之同根：一个专心工作的地方。

normal.en: Compare diligent: diligent stresses hard work, studious stresses devotion to learning.
normal.cn: 对比 diligent：diligent 强调肯下苦功，studious 强调一心向学。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that stays on long after the rest of the house has gone dark.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，满屋都黑了之后它还亮着。

abstract.en: Imagine a notebook filled so neatly that the margins are used too.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记得极整齐的笔记本，连页边都写满了。

abstract.en: Think of a person who pauses to check every sign twice out of sheer care.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人出于极致的用心，每个标识都要看两遍。

examples.en: He was studious enough to finish the whole course in one term.
examples.cn: 他用功到在一个学期内就学完了整门课。

examples.en: The studious girl kept a notebook of new words.
examples.cn: 那个好学的女孩有一本新词笔记。

examples.en: They made a studious effort to avoid mentioning the failure.
examples.cn: 他们刻意地避免提到那次失败。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死丢的耶思」——书一到手就拼命钻研，连思考都舍不得丢；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 studium（热切的追求、钻研）→ studiosus（热切的、专心的）→ 古法语 studieus → 英语 studious；同根词有 study、student、studio，核心义「一心向学」。

sensesIntro.en: Studious begins with a person given over to books, widens to steady effort of any kind, and ends with careful deliberate action.
sensesIntro.cn: studious 先指一心扑在书上的人，再扩展到任何形式的踏实努力，最后落到细致而有意的行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning late over a page covered in notes.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜深了，灯还亮着，书页上写满笔记。

branches.en: A person devoted to books is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 一心读书的人是日常义项。

branches.en: Effort in any field becomes diligence.
branches.cn: 把用功移到任何领域，就是勤勉。

branches.en: Careful attention turns effort into something deliberate.
branches.cn: 仔细的留意把努力变成刻意的行动。

branches.en: Study habits and general hard work grow from the same zeal.
branches.cn: 学习习惯与一般的肯下苦功，出自同一股热忱。

branches.en: A person can work hard at not doing something, and that effort is studious too.
branches.cn: 一个人也可以努力避免做某事，那种努力同样可以称为 studious。

intro.en: Studious adds the adjective ending -ous to the Latin stem studi-, also found in study and student.
intro.cn: studious 在拉丁词干 studi- 上加形容词词尾 -ous 构成，study 与 student 也出自同一词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin studium and studiosus give English study, student, and studious.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 studium 与 studiosus 给出英语的 study、student 与 studious。

items.example: Studium names the zeal behind study.
items.exampleCN: studium 指学习背后的热忱。

items.example: Studiosus is the direct model for the English word.
items.exampleCN: studiosus 是英语词的直接模板。

items.example: The suffix -ous means full of.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 表示充满。

items.example: Study is the plain verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: study 是这一词族的朴素动词。

items.example: Student names the person who studies.
items.exampleCN: student 指学习的人。

items.example: Studio arrived through Italian and keeps the sense of a room for work.
items.exampleCN: studio 经意大利语传入，保留了「工作之室」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms studiously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 studiously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms studiousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 studiousness。

items.example: The adjective keeps the zealous core.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词保留了「热切」的核心。

definition_zh: 通风不好的；闷热的；（鼻子）不通气的；一本正经的；拘谨守旧的；无聊沉闷的
definition_en: lacking fresh air; also used of a blocked nose, and of a person, place, or manner that is dull, formal, or afraid of new ideas
core_image: 门窗紧关的小房间里，空气与新鲜想法都透不进来
scene: 会议室关了窗，人又多，空气很快变得闷人。With the windows shut and so many people inside, the meeting room soon turned stuffy.
sceneCN: 这里 stuffy 是「空气不流通、发闷」（第 1 个义项）；句意：会议室关了窗，人又多，空气很快变得发闷。

pos.zh: 通风不好的；闷热的
鼻子不通气的；鼻塞的
一本正经的；拘谨守旧的；无聊的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「闷热；闷气；拘谨」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「拘谨地；古板地」
基础动词，义为「填塞；塞满」；stuffiness 的核心画面正是「空气被填满了」
由否定前缀 un- 与 stuffy 构成，义为「不拘谨的；随和的」

senses.title: Lacking fresh air
senses.definition: having warm, stale air and no fresh breeze
senses.definitionCN: 空气温暖污浊、没有新鲜的风吹进来
senses.example: The train was hot and stuffy after an hour by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 在海边开了一个小时后，车厢里又热又闷。
senses.why: The base word stuff means to pack something full, and a stuffy room is a space packed so full that the air cannot move.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词 stuff 意为「塞满」，闷的房间就是被塞满到空气无法流动的空间，这正是核心意象。

senses.title: A blocked nose
senses.definition: having a nose that is full of mucus and cannot breathe freely
senses.definitionCN: 鼻腔被分泌物堵住、呼吸不畅
senses.example: I have a stuffy nose and a sore throat.
senses.exampleCN: 我鼻子塞，喉咙也痛。
senses.why: The same idea of being packed or blocked moves from a room to a nose, where the airway is filled up.
senses.whyCN: 「被填塞」的画面从房间挪到鼻腔：通道被塞住了，呼吸就不顺，与闷室的堵塞感同源。

senses.title: Old-fashioned and dull
senses.definition: too formal, strict, or old-fashioned, with no room for new ideas
senses.definitionCN: 过分正式、刻板或守旧，容不下新想法
senses.example: Her grandparents hold rather stuffy views about the family business.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母对家族生意持有相当古板的看法。
senses.why: A mind packed with rigid rules lets nothing new drift in, just as a shut room keeps out the fresh air.
senses.whyCN: 头脑被刻板规矩塞满，新想法就飘不进来，和关紧窗户的房间进不了新鲜空气一样，这是从具体到抽象的延伸。

senses.title: Hot and humid
senses.definition: unpleasantly warm and humid, with the air feeling heavy
senses.definitionCN: 又热又潮湿，空气沉重难受
senses.example: It was a stuffy evening before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨前是一个闷热的傍晚。
senses.why: When warm damp air cannot escape, heat collects, so a stuffy place is also a hot and heavy one.
senses.whyCN: 暖湿空气散不出去，热气就积在里面，所以闷的空间同时又是闷热的地方，热度是通风差带来的结果。

senses.title: Dull and boring
senses.definition: lacking interest or excitement, often because events are over-formal
senses.definitionCN: 缺少趣味和刺激，常因活动过于正式
senses.example: The annual dinner was long and stuffy.
senses.exampleCN: 年会长而沉闷。
senses.why: Anything over-formal and packed with ceremony leaves no room for surprise or fun, which we call boring.
senses.whyCN: 过度正式、被仪式塞满的场合容不下惊喜与乐趣，于是变得无聊，这是「填满而无法流动」在气氛层面的延伸。

senses.title: An atmosphere of constraint
senses.definition: a social mood in which people feel stiff, cautious, or trapped
senses.definitionCN: 人们感到拘束、谨慎或喘不过气的社交气氛
senses.example: There was a stuffy silence when she raised the question.
senses.exampleCN: 她提出这个问题时，场面一片压抑的沉默。
senses.why: Feelings can stay shut in just like air: when nothing is breathed out, a tense silence descends.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也能像空气一样被关在屋里：谁都不肯呼气开口，沉默就压下来，这是闷「空气」与闷「情绪」的合体。

senses.title: Conventional in taste
senses.definition: preferring familiar, conventional styles and showing no taste for the new
senses.definitionCN: 偏爱熟悉保守的样式，对新潮流毫无兴趣
senses.example: The magazine has a slightly stuffy, old-school style.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志风格略带古板的老派气息。
senses.why: The abstract sense extends to style and taste: a stuffy magazine feels closed to new air.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义再延伸到风格与品味：古板的杂志给人的感觉是「对新空气关着门」。

senses.title: Not forward-looking
senses.definition: used of an institution that resists change and new thinking
senses.definitionCN: 形容抵制变革与新颖思想的机构
senses.example: Critics called the university a stuffy institution.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这所大学是个保守僵化的机构。
senses.why: When a body of people shares the same closed, rule-filled outlook, the word moves onto the institution itself.
senses.whyCN: 当一群人都怀着同一种封闭、塞满规矩的心态时，这个词就挪来形容机构本身，语义升格。

intro.en: Stuffy grows out of stuff, the verb meaning to pack full. A place packed full has no air left to move, which gives the sense of stifling and later the sense of rigid and old-fashioned.
intro.cn: stuffy 由动词 stuff（塞满）派生而来。被塞满的地方没有空气可以流动，于是产生「闷」的含义，后来再引申出「古板守旧」。

items.en: Estoffe names the material or stock that something is made from.
items.cn: estoffe 指做某物所用的材料或货品。

items.en: Middle English stuff comes from French and means material or a supply of goods.
items.cn: 中古英语 stuff 借自法语，意为材料或货物。

items.en: The verb to stuff develops the sense of filling a thing tightly with material.
items.cn: 动词 stuff 发展出「用材料塞满」的含义。

items.en: The adjective stuffy is recorded, meaning full of stuff or lacking fresh air.
items.cn: 形容词 stuffy 见于记载，意为「充满东西的、缺少新鲜空气的」。

items.en: The word extends to noses that are blocked and to people who are stiff in manner.
items.cn: 词义延伸到堵塞的鼻子以及举止生硬的人。

items.en: Stuffy now also describes dull, conservative, and badly ventilated spaces.
items.cn: 现代英语中 stuffy 还形容沉闷、保守以及通风很差的空间。

note.en: Stuffy sits beside its own family of stuff, stuffiness, and stuffily, and beside air words such as stifling and stale.
note.cn: stuffy 与同族的 stuff、stuffiness、stuffily 相邻，也与 stifling、stale 这类「空气」词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 塞满；填装

entries.definition: the state of having bad air or a blocked nose
entries.definitionCN: 闷热；鼻塞；拘谨

entries.definition: filled completely, or full after eating
entries.definitionCN: 塞满的；吃得过饱的

entries.definition: material used to fill something, such as a cushion
entries.definitionCN: 填塞物；馅料

entries.definition: so hot or airless that it is hard to breathe

entries.definition: having a good supply of fresh air
