entries.definition: smelling old and damp, or very old-fashioned
entries.definitionCN: 有霉味的；陈旧过时的

normalIntro.en: Stuffy is the adjective of stuffing: when a space, a nose, or a mind is packed full, nothing fresh can move through it.
normalIntro.cn: stuffy 是 stuff（塞）的形容词：空间、鼻子或头脑被塞满时，新鲜的东西就流动不起来。

normal.en: The suffix -y turns the verb stuff into an adjective meaning full of stuff.
normal.cn: 后缀 -y 把动词 stuff 变成表示「充满某物」的形容词。

normal.en: A stuffy room is the opposite of a well-ventilated room.
normal.cn: stuffy room 与 a well-ventilated room（通风好的房间）正相反。

normal.en: A stuffy nose is blocked by mucus, so call it a blocked nose in plain speech.
normal.cn: stuffy nose 指被分泌物堵住的鼻子，日常也可以直接说 blocked nose。

normal.en: The noun form is stuffiness, and the adverb form is stuffily.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 stuffiness，副词形式是 stuffily。

normal.en: For people, compare informal and relaxed: a stuffy host keeps the party strict.
normal.cn: 形容人时对比 informal 与 relaxed：stuffy 的主人会把宴会办得很拘束。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed holiday parcel box on a summer day.
abstract.cn: 想象夏天里一只封死的纸箱，闷得让人发慌。

abstract.en: Think of a senior club where every member sits in identical suits.
abstract.cn: 想象一个老俱乐部，每位成员都穿着同款西装正襟危坐。

abstract.en: Hear a voice politely asking you to close the window again.
abstract.cn: 听见有人客气地再一次请你把窗户关上。

examples.en: The attic bedroom was stuffy, so we opened every window.
examples.cn: 阁楼卧室很闷，于是我们把每扇窗都打开了。

examples.en: A stuffy nose kept me awake all night.
examples.cn: 鼻塞让我整夜没睡着。

examples.en: He found the club too stuffy for his taste.
examples.cn: 他觉得这个俱乐部对他的口味来说太拘谨守旧了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死打非」——门窗关死、热度打不散，非得闷出毛病；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 estoffe（材料、货品）→ 中古英语 stuff（材料）与动词 stuff（塞满）→ 加后缀 -y 成 stuffy（充满的；缺新鲜空气的），核心义「被塞满而无法流动」。

sensesIntro.en: Stuffy starts from the physical sense of packed, stale air, spreads to a blocked nose, and then moves to mind and manner: rules and ideas that cannot move.
sensesIntro.cn: stuffy 从「被塞满、空气不流通」的实体含义出发，先延伸到鼻塞，再转向头脑与做派：规矩和想法都流不动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed small room where the air, and the new ideas, cannot get in or out.
core.cn: 核心意象：门窗紧闭的小房间，空气进不来也出不去，新鲜想法同样如此。

branches.en: The airless room is the first and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 闷室是第一个、也最字面的义项。

branches.en: A blocked airway carries the packing image to the nose.
branches.cn: 堵塞的呼吸道把「填塞」画面带到鼻子。

branches.en: Heat building up in stale air gives the hot and humid sense.
branches.cn: 浊气中积聚的热量带来闷热义。

branches.en: Rules, taste, and institutions can also be shut against new air.
branches.cn: 规矩、品味和机构同样会对新鲜空气关上门。

branches.en: Over-formal events and tense silences both leave no room to breathe.
branches.cn: 过度正式的场合与紧绷的沉默都让人透不过气。

intro.en: Stuffy is built on the English noun and verb stuff plus the adjective suffix -y, and it forms stuffiness, stuffily, and unstuffy.
intro.cn: stuffy 由英语名词兼动词 stuff 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，再派生 stuffiness、stuffily 与 unstuffy。

latinIntro.en: Stuffy has no Latin elements of its own; its base stuff reached English through Old French from a Germanic root, listed here only as background.
latinIntro.cn: stuffy 本身不含拉丁词素；它的基础词 stuff 经古法语进入英语，源头是日耳曼语，这里只作背景列出。

items.example: Stuff the pillow with feathers.
items.exampleCN: 用羽毛把枕头塞满。

items.meaning: material or a collection of things
items.example: Take that stuff off the table.
items.exampleCN: 把桌上的东西拿走。

items.example: A stuffy classroom makes pupils sleepy.
items.exampleCN: 闷气的教室让学生犯困。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.meaningCN: 充满……的；具有……性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -y forms stuffy from stuff.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 由 stuff 构成 stuffy。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms stuffiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 stuffiness。

items.meaning: the state of having bad air or a blocked nose
items.example: Stuffiness in the cabin worried the nurse.
items.exampleCN: 机舱里的闷气让护士担心。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms stuffily.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 stuffily。

items.meaning: in a stiff or old-fashioned way
items.example: He spoke stuffily about modern art.
items.exampleCN: 他古板地评论现代艺术。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unstuffy.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unstuffy。

items.meaning: informal and open to new ideas
items.example: Her writing is lively and unstuffy.
items.exampleCN: 她的文字生动又不拘谨。

definition_zh: 使震惊；使目瞪口呆；把……打晕；使昏厥；（声音）震聋；使（某物）失去功能
definition_en: to shock someone so strongly that they cannot think or speak, and also to make a person or animal unconscious by a blow or an electric charge
core_image: 一记重击落下，雷声般的轰响把人的意识震得一片空白
scene: 那则消息来得太突然，所有人都说不出一句话。The news came so suddenly that everyone in the room was completely stunned.
sceneCN: 这里 stunned 是「惊呆、震惊」（第 1 个义项）；句意：那则消息来得太突然，房间里所有人都被惊呆了。

pos.zh: 使震惊；使目瞪口呆
把……打晕；使昏厥
（声音）震聋；使失去知觉

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转成的形容词，义为「惊人的；极美的；令人震撼的」
由动词加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「令人惊叹的人或物」
由 stun 与 gun 组成的复合名词，义为「电击枪」
由过去分词转成的形容词，义为「震惊的；目瞪口呆的」

senses.title: To shock someone deeply
senses.definition: to surprise or shock someone so much that they cannot think clearly or react
senses.definitionCN: 让人惊讶或震撼到无法思考或反应
senses.example: The court verdict stunned the whole nation.
senses.exampleCN: 法院的裁决震惊了全国。
senses.why: The old sense is to knock the senses out of someone, and sudden news can strike the mind the way a blow strikes the head.
senses.whyCN: 古义是把人的知觉「打掉」，突发的消息像一击打在头上，脑子瞬间空白，这就是核心意象的抽象化。

senses.title: To make unconscious by a blow
senses.definition: to hit someone or something so hard that they lose consciousness
senses.definitionCN: 重重一击使人失去意识
senses.example: A heavy branch stunned the climber for a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 一根粗树枝把登山者打晕了几秒钟。
senses.why: This is the most physical core of the word: a blow lands and the person goes out like a light.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的核心义：一记重击落下，人像灯一样一下子灭了。

senses.title: To knock out with electricity
senses.definition: to use an electric charge to make a person or animal unable to move
senses.definitionCN: 用电击使人或动物无法动弹
senses.example: The vet stuns the cattle briefly before the examination.
senses.exampleCN: 兽医在检查前先把牛短暂电晕。
senses.why: Electricity now does the knocking, so the same loss of control comes from a current instead of a club.
senses.whyCN: 现在由电流代替木棒来完成「击倒」，那种失去自控的状态不变，只是工具换了。

senses.title: To deafen someone with noise
senses.definition: to make someone unable to hear for a moment because of a very loud sound
senses.definitionCN: 巨大的声响让人一时听不见
senses.example: The explosion stunned the miners and they could not hear the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 爆炸把矿工们震得耳鸣，他们听不到警报。
senses.why: The earliest Latin sense is a thunderclap, and a thunderclap takes hearing away, so loudness alone can stun.
senses.whyCN: 最早的拉丁语含义与雷声有关，雷声会夺走听觉，所以仅凭巨响也足以让人发懵。

senses.title: To amaze with beauty or quality
senses.titleCN: 令人赞叹；美得让人惊叹
senses.definition: to hold someone in admiration because something is very beautiful or impressive
senses.definitionCN: 因某事非常美或非常了不起而令人赞叹
senses.example: The sunset over the lake stuns every visitor.
senses.exampleCN: 湖上的日落让每位游客叹为观止。
senses.why: Shock can be delightful too: beauty overwhelms the senses in the same way shock does, just without fear.
senses.whyCN: 震惊也可以是愉悦的：美以同样的力量冲垮感官，只是不带恐惧，这就是「震撼」的正面用法。

senses.title: To stop a process abruptly
senses.definition: to stop a person, plant, or process suddenly before it can go on
senses.definitionCN: 在人、植物或过程还没来得及继续时使其骤然停止
senses.example: A sudden frost can stun young shoots.
senses.exampleCN: 突降的严霜能让幼苗停止生长。
senses.why: A stun effect blocks normal activity, so anything that is suddenly checked can be said to be stunned.
senses.whyCN: stun 的效果是让正常活动停住，所以任何被突然遏制的东西都可以说被「击晕」或「震住」。

senses.title: To stun a fish or animal
senses.definition: to disable fish or small animals so they can be caught without being killed at once
senses.definitionCN: 把鱼或小动物弄晕，以便当场捕获
senses.example: Some fishers stun the fish with a small electric current.
senses.exampleCN: 有些渔民用微弱电流把鱼电晕。
senses.why: The practical sense grew from hunting and fishing with clubs, where stunning came before catching.
senses.whyCN: 这一实用义源自用木棒捕猎捕鱼的旧法：先弄晕再抓，是核心义在劳作场景中的落地。

senses.title: To surprise completely
senses.definition: used informally for an unexpected turn of events that leaves people speechless
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容意外的转折让人一时说不出话
senses.example: The final goal stunned the home crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一粒进球让主场观众大吃一惊。
senses.why: In everyday speech the strong shock sense softens into plain surprise, still with a moment of frozen reaction.
senses.whyCN: 在日常口语里，强烈的震惊褪成一般的惊讶，但「怔住一瞬」的反应仍在。

intro.en: Stun comes through Old French from Latin tonare, to thunder. The earliest English sense is close to being deafened or knocked senseless, as if by a thunderclap.
intro.cn: stun 经古法语进入英语，源头是拉丁语 tonare（打雷）。英语最早的含义接近「被雷声震得失聪或失去知觉」。

items.en: Tonare means to thunder, and the noun tonitrus names a thunderclap.
items.cn: tonare 意为打雷，名词 tonitrus 指雷声。

items.en: A spoken Latin verb form built on tonare develops the sense of producing a thunderous sound.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语中，以 tonare 为基础的一个动词形式发展出「发出雷鸣般巨响」的意思。

items.en: Estoner means to make a loud noise like thunder and to make someone senseless.
items.cn: estoner 意为发出雷鸣般的巨响，并「使人失去知觉、发懵」。

items.en: The English verb stun first describes being deprived of hearing or feeling by a blow or a loud noise.
items.cn: 英语动词 stun 最初描述因打击或巨响而失去听觉或感觉。

items.en: The physical knocking sense is applied to fishing and hunting, and is later extended to the mind.
items.cn: 「击晕」的实体义被用于捕鱼和狩猎，随后扩展到心智层面。

items.en: Stun covers sudden shock, electric stunning devices, and the admiring sense in stunning.
items.cn: 现代英语中 stun 兼指突发的震惊、电击麻醉装置，以及 stunning 中的赞叹之义。

note.en: Stun belongs to a family with stunning, stunned, and stunner, and stands close to shock, astound, and daze, though stun carries a stronger physical image.
note.cn: stun 与 stunning、stunned、stunner 同族，近义上有 shock、astound、daze，但 stun 带有更强的「击打」实体意象。

entries.definition: extremely impressive or extremely beautiful
entries.definitionCN: 极美的；令人震撼的

entries.definition: so shocked that one cannot move or speak
entries.definitionCN: 惊呆的；目瞪口呆的

entries.definition: a very beautiful person or a very impressive thing
entries.definitionCN: 极美的人；令人惊叹的事物

entries.definition: the loud noise that follows lightning
entries.definitionCN: 雷声；雷

entries.definition: to make someone feel very upset or surprised
entries.definitionCN: 使震惊；使不安

entries.definition: to shock someone with something very surprising
entries.definitionCN: 使惊愕；使大吃一惊

entries.definition: to make someone unable to think clearly
entries.definitionCN: 使发懵；使迷糊

normalIntro.en: Stun keeps a thunderclap inside it: a bang so loud and sudden that the head goes blank for a moment.
normalIntro.cn: stun 里藏着一记雷声：响得突然，脑子瞬间一片空白。

normal.en: The Latin root tonare means to thunder, which links stun to thunder and thunderous.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 tonare 意为打雷，把 stun 与 thunder、thunderous 连在一起。

normal.en: Be stunned by is the usual passive pattern for news that leaves someone speechless.
normal.cn: be stunned by 是描述「被消息惊呆」的常用被动句式。

normal.en: The present participle stunning is one of the word family members that means very impressive.
normal.cn: 现在分词 stunning 是同族成员之一，意为「令人赞叹」。

normal.en: A stun gun delivers an electric charge, so it uses the electric sense of the verb.
normal.cn: stun gun 通过放电工作，用的是动词的「电击」义。

normal.en: The compound stun gun names the device, while stunning describes the effect on people.
normal.cn: 复合词 stun gun 指装置本身，而 stunning 描述对人所产生的效果。

abstract.en: Picture a bright flash and the next second being all white noise.
abstract.cn: 想象一道强光闪过，下一瞬只剩满耳的嗡鸣，分辨不出任何声音。

abstract.en: Imagine reading one short message that freezes you in mid-step.
abstract.cn: 想象读到一条很短的短信，人就此定在半路，忘了要往哪走。

abstract.en: Think of standing still on the stage while the crowd slowly applauds.
abstract.cn: 想象站在台上动弹不得，台下观众慢慢鼓起掌来。

examples.en: The discovery stunned the scientific community.
examples.cn: 这一发现震惊了科学界。

examples.en: Riot police used stun grenades and tear gas.
examples.cn: 防暴警察使用了震撼弹和催泪瓦斯。

examples.en: She was too stunned to answer immediately.
examples.cn: 她惊得一时答不上话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「死盾」——一记闷棍打在盾上，人当场被震晕；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 tonare（打雷）→ 通俗拉丁语「发出雷鸣般巨响」的动词 → 古法语 estoner（震响；使人发懵）→ 中古英语 stun（震得失聪、打晕）→ 现代英语「使震惊」。

sensesIntro.en: Stun begins with a thunderclap that shuts down hearing and thought, spreads to physical knocking-out by a blow or a current, and then widens into shock and astonishment.
sensesIntro.cn: stun 从一记「关掉听觉与思考」的雷声开始，扩展到用棍棒或电流把人打晕，再扩大到震惊与惊叹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy knock, like a thunderclap, that empties the head for a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：一记沉重的击打，如雷声般让头脑瞬间一片空白。

branches.en: The frozen mind is the main abstract sense.
branches.cn: 头脑空白是最主要的抽象义。

branches.en: Blows, currents, and fishing tackle all deliver the physical knock.
branches.cn: 打击、电流与捕鱼器具都完成这记实体重击。

branches.en: Loud sound keeps the oldest thunder sense alive.
branches.cn: 巨大声响延续了最古老的雷声义。

branches.en: Overwhelming beauty or sudden events both freeze the thoughts.
branches.cn: 压倒性的美与突发事件都会让思维冻结。

branches.en: Any process that is abruptly checked is said to be stunned.
branches.cn: 任何被突然遏止的过程都可用 stun 形容。

intro.en: Stun is a whole-word verb with no productive affix of its own; it is learned through its family members stunning, stunned, stunner, and the compound stun gun.
intro.cn: stun 是整体习得的动词，本身不含能产词缀；它通过 stunning、stunned、stunner 以及复合词 stun gun 形成词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin background is tonare, to thunder, behind Old French estoner; the English word lost the initial e- on the way in.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语背景是 tonare（打雷），处在古法语 estoner 背后；进入英语时开头的 e- 脱落了。

items.example: The price will stun most buyers.
items.exampleCN: 这个价格会让大多数买家目瞪口呆。

items.example: Each new finding stuns the press.
items.exampleCN: 每项新发现都让媒体震惊。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去式与过去分词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ed forms stunned.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 stunned。

items.meaning: present participle and act of doing
items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词与动名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ing forms stunning.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 stunning。

items.example: They built a stunning house by the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们在海边建了一座漂亮的房子。

items.example: The fans sat stunned after the final whistle.
items.exampleCN: 终场哨响后，球迷们坐在那里发呆。

items.meaning: a person or thing that does something
items.meaningCN: 表示施事者或事物名称的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -er forms stunner.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 stunner。

items.meaning: a very beautiful or impressive thing
items.meaningCN: 极美的人或物；令人叫绝的事物
items.example: Her last film was a stunner.
items.exampleCN: 她的上一部电影令人叫绝。

items.example: The guard carried a stun gun.
items.exampleCN: 保安带着一把电击枪。

latinEntries.example: Tonare is the thunder behind estoner.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tonare 是 estoner 背后的「雷声」。

latinEntries.meaning: to stun or make senseless with noise
latinEntries.example: Estoner was taken into English as stun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: estoner 进入英语成为 stun。

latinEntries.example: Tonitrus keeps the sound image in Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tonitrus 在拉丁语里保留了声响意象。

definition_zh: 时髦的；有型的；有品味的；漂亮雅致的
definition_en: looking attractive because of good design, taste, and a sense of current fashion
core_image: 一个从帽子到鞋都搭配得恰到好处的人走在街上，路人纷纷回头
scene: 她穿一件剪裁利落的深色大衣，看上去非常有型。In a sharply cut dark coat, she looked remarkably stylish.
sceneCN: 这里 stylish 是「时髦、有型的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她穿一件剪裁利落的深色大衣，看上去非常有型。

pos.zh: 时髦的；有型的
有品味的；雅致的

forms.label: 比较级（多用 more 构成）
最高级（多用 most 构成）

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「时髦地；有型地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「时髦；有品味」
基础名词，义为「风格；款式」，stylish 正是「有风格」的形象说法
由 style 加施事后缀 -ist 构成，义为「造型师；时装设计师」

senses.title: Fashionable in clothing
senses.definition: wearing or made of clothes that look modern, well chosen, and attractive
senses.definitionCN: 穿着或制作得现代、搭配得当而好看的衣服
senses.example: He has become a stylish dresser since moving to Milan.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到米兰之后，他变得格外会穿。
senses.why: Style is the noun for a personal way of doing or wearing something, so stylish means someone who has a recognisable, attractive way.
senses.whyCN: style 指个人做事或穿着的「方式」，所以 stylish 就是「有自己的、好看的方式」，核心意象落在身上。

senses.title: Elegant in design
senses.definition: used of objects, rooms, or products that are well designed and pleasing to look at
senses.definitionCN: 形容设计精良、看起来令人愉悦的物品、房间或产品
senses.example: The room was simple but very stylish.
senses.exampleCN: 房间简朴，却非常有品位。
senses.why: The same taste can live in things, not just people: a chair or a room can carry a good style.
senses.whyCN: 同一种品味不仅住在人身上，也住在物件里：一把椅子、一间房都能有好的「风格」。

senses.title: Showing good taste
senses.definition: having a collection of clothes, objects, or habits that reveal a confident sense of taste
senses.definitionCN: 衣物、物件或习惯体现出自信而良好的审美
senses.example: She keeps a stylish flat full of old furniture.
senses.exampleCN: 她把一间摆满旧家具的房子打理得很有品味。
senses.why: Fashion is what is popular now, but taste judges what is fitting, so stylish holds both the current and the tasteful.
senses.whyCN: 时尚说的是「现在流行什么」，品味判断的是「什么合适」，stylish 把两者都装在身上。

senses.title: Lively and graceful
senses.definition: describing a manner of moving, speaking, or behaving that is smooth and pleasing
senses.definitionCN: 形容动作、谈吐或举止流畅而讨人喜欢
senses.example: He made a stylish speech that nobody forgot.
senses.exampleCN: 他发表了一场令人难忘的漂亮演讲。
senses.why: Style governs how a thing is done as well as how it looks, so stylish extends from the body to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 风格既管「看起来怎样」，也管「做起来怎样」，于是 stylish 从外表延伸到行为举止。

senses.title: Smart and modern
senses.definition: used of shops, hotels, and neighbourhoods that are modern, fashionable, and pricey
senses.definitionCN: 形容现代、时髦而价格偏高的商店、酒店与街区
senses.example: The old street is now full of stylish hotels.
senses.exampleCN: 那条老街如今满是时髦的酒店。
senses.why: Fashionable people gather in fashionable places, so a whole district can be judged by its style.
senses.whyCN: 时髦的人汇聚在时髦的地方，于是整片街区也会被用「风格」来评判。

senses.title: For fashion followers
senses.definition: often used of people who actively follow current fashion and trends
senses.definitionCN: 常形容主动追随潮流与时尚的人
senses.example: The magazine is aimed at youthful, stylish readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志面向年轻而讲究潮流的读者。
senses.why: When the suffix marks a group of people, stylish can describe the kind of audience who follow new trends.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词用来标记一群人时，stylish 就形容追逐新潮的那类受众。

senses.title: Smart in its presentation
senses.definition: used of a display, layout, or presentation that is neat, attractive, and well arranged
senses.definitionCN: 形容陈列、版面或展示整洁美观、安排得当
senses.example: They put together a stylish brochure for the exhibition.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为展览做了一本漂亮的手册。
senses.why: Good style also means good arrangement, so a page or a window display can be stylish.
senses.whyCN: 好的风格也意味着好的安排，于是版面或橱窗陈列同样可以「有型」。

senses.title: Done with flair
senses.definition: describing a skill or technique performed with skill and flair rather than only for practical effect
senses.definitionCN: 以熟练而潇洒的方式完成技艺，而不只求实用
senses.example: The striker finished the match with a stylish left foot.
senses.exampleCN: 那名前锋用娴熟的左脚射门结束了比赛。
senses.why: From personal style the word reaches performance: skill with flair is style in motion.
senses.whyCN: 从个人风格走向表演与技艺：带着潇洒的熟练，就是动起来的风格。

intro.en: Stylish is an English formation on the noun style, which came from Latin stilus, the pointed instrument used for writing on wax tablets.
intro.cn: stylish 是英语内部由名词 style 构成的词，而 style 来自拉丁语 stilus，即用来在蜡板上写字的尖笔。

items.en: Stilus is a pointed writing instrument, and also comes to mean a way of writing.
items.cn: stilus 是一种尖头写字工具，后来也指书写的方式。

items.en: Stylle enters French with the sense of a way of writing and of manner.
items.cn: stylle 进入法语，指书写方式与做法、风度。

items.en: Style in English first names a writer or a manner of writing, and later fashion in dress.
items.cn: 英语 style 最初指写作者或写作方式，后来也指穿着时尚。

items.en: The adjective stylish is recorded describing clothes, manners, and design that show good fashion and taste.
items.cn: 形容词 stylish 见于记载，用来形容体现良好时尚与品味的衣服、举止和设计。

items.en: Printing and advertising extend style to visual layout and presentation.
items.cn: 印刷与广告业把 style 扩展到版面与展示的视觉安排。

items.en: Stylish and styled now cover fashion, interior design, products, and performance.
items.cn: 现代英语中 stylish 与 styled 覆盖时尚、室内设计、产品与技艺表现。

note.en: Stylish is built on style and shares a family with stylishly and stylishness; it stands close to elegant, chic, and fashionable.
note.cn: stylish 建立在 style 之上，与 stylishly、stylishness 同族，近义上有 elegant、chic、fashionable。

entries.definition: a way of doing, making, or dressing that is someone own
entries.definitionCN: 某人独有的做事、制作或穿着方式

entries.definition: made or arranged in a particular style
entries.definitionCN: 按某种风格制作或布置的

entries.definition: the way something is designed or arranged
entries.definitionCN: 造型；设计风格

entries.definition: a person who arranges hair or clothes for a fashion or show setting
entries.definitionCN: 造型师；时装设计师

entries.definition: graceful and attractive in appearance or manner
entries.definitionCN: 优雅的；雅致的

entries.definition: stylish in a way that shows good fashion taste
entries.definitionCN: 时髦的；有格调的

entries.definition: popular at a particular time
entries.definitionCN: 流行的；时尚的

normalIntro.en: Stylish is style plus the suffix -ish: having the quality of having a style.
normalIntro.cn: stylish 是 style 加后缀 -ish：具有「有风格」这一性质的。

normal.en: The suffix -ish usually means having the quality of, as in stylish, foolish, and childish.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ish 通常表示「有……性质的」，如 stylish、foolish、childish。

normal.en: The noun is stylishness and the adverb is stylishly.
normal.cn: 名词是 stylishness，副词是 stylishly。

normal.en: Compare fashionable and stylish: fashionable follows trends, while stylish also praises taste.
normal.cn: 对比 fashionable 与 stylish：前者跟随潮流，后者还赞美品味。

normal.en: For pieces of writing compare plain and elegant, and for designs compare simple and stylish.
normal.cn: 谈文字时对比 plain 与 elegant，谈设计时对比 simple 与 stylish。

normal.en: The verb style means to design or arrange something in a particular way.
normal.cn: 动词 style 意为按某种方式设计或布置。

abstract.en: Picture a person walking past a shop window and stopping to look.
abstract.cn: 想象一个走过橱窗的人停下来多看了一眼。

abstract.en: Imagine one well-chosen scarf tied in one perfect loop.
abstract.cn: 想象一条选得极好的围巾，只打了一个完美的圈。

abstract.en: Think of an old theatre programme that looks newly printed.
abstract.cn: 想象一份老剧院的节目单，看起来却像刚印的一样漂亮。

examples.en: They transformed the old warehouse into a stylish restaurant.
examples.cn: 他们把旧仓库改造成一家有品位的餐厅。

examples.en: A stylish jacket can be worth more than a costly one.
examples.cn: 一件有型的夹克可能比一件很贵的夹克更值。

examples.en: She writes in a clear and stylish way.
examples.cn: 她的文字清晰而漂亮。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「斯呆立士」——翻成「绅士」，绅士穿得有型、走得体面；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 stilus（蜡板上的尖笔；书写方式）→ 古法语 stylle（写法；风度）→ 英语 style（风格；款式）→ 加后缀 -ish 成 stylish（有风格、有品味的），核心义「有自己的一套好样子」。

sensesIntro.en: Stylish grows from the body outward: from clothes and objects to taste, manners, places, presentations, and finally the flair of a performance.
sensesIntro.cn: stylish 从人身上向外长：从衣服和物件扩到品味、举止、场所、展示，最后落到技艺的潇洒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person whose whole outfit, from hat to shoes, is chosen with perfect sense.
core.cn: 核心意象：从帽子到鞋子都搭配得恰到好处的人。

branches.en: Clothing is where stylish first and most often lives.
branches.cn: 衣着是 stylish 最常落脚的地方。

branches.en: Design carries the same judgement onto objects and rooms.
branches.cn: 同样的判断也用在物件与房间的设计上。

branches.en: Taste and trend-following are the two sides of the adjective at home.
branches.cn: 品味与追潮流是这个形容词的两面。

branches.en: Behaving and performing with flair extends style to action.
branches.cn: 带着风度的举止与技艺把风格延伸到行动。

branches.en: A modern district and a clean layout both show good design.
branches.cn: 现代街区与整洁版面都体现好的设计。

intro.en: Stylish is style plus the adjective suffix -ish, and it forms stylishly and stylishness.
intro.cn: stylish 是 style 加形容词后缀 -ish，再派生 stylishly 与 stylishness。

latinIntro.en: Style comes from Latin stilus, a pointed pen for wax tablets; the pen image is the seed of a way of writing, then of doing things, then of dressing.
latinIntro.cn: style 来自拉丁语 stilus，即书写蜡板用的尖笔；这支笔的形象是「写法」，再是「做法」，最后是「穿法」的种子。

items.meaning: a particular way of doing, dressing, or making
items.example: Her style is simple and bold.
items.exampleCN: 她的风格简约而大胆。

items.meaning: to design or arrange in a certain way
items.example: They styled the room with old lamps.
items.exampleCN: 他们用旧灯装饰了房间。

items.example: The suffix -ish forms stylish from style.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 由 style 构成 stylish。

items.example: The cover looks modern and stylish.
items.exampleCN: 封面看上去现代而有型。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms stylishly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 stylishly。

items.meaning: in a fashionable and tasteful way
items.example: She dressed stylishly for the opening night.
items.exampleCN: 首演当晚她穿得很时髦。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms stylishness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 stylishness。

items.meaning: the quality of being fashionable and tasteful
items.example: Stylishness is a matter of small choices.
items.exampleCN: 时髦与否取决于无数细小的选择。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms stylist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 stylist。

items.meaning: a person who arranges styles for fashion, hair, or writing
items.meaningCN: 造型师；时装设计师；文体家
items.example: A stylist chose every jacket for the shoot.
items.exampleCN: 一位造型师为拍摄挑选了每件外套。

latinEntries.meaning: a pointed pen for writing on wax
latinEntries.example: Stilus links the pen to the idea of manner.
latinEntries.exampleCN: stilus 把「笔」与「做法」联系起来。

latinEntries.meaning: a way of writing or a manner
latinEntries.example: Style was borrowed into English from French.

latinEntries.meaning: belonging to or having the nature of
latinEntries.example: The suffix -ish is native English, not Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 后缀 -ish 是英语本土词素，并非拉丁来源。

definition_zh: 主观的；主观性的；受个人情感或看法影响的；（语法）主格的；以主语形式出现的
definition_en: based on the feelings, tastes or viewpoint of one particular person rather than on facts that anyone can check
core_image: 同一幅画前，甲看见暖意，乙看见寒意；画布没变，画里多了一双各自的眼
scene: 两位评审看同一份草案，一位说清晰有力，另一位说含糊混乱，他们没有拿出任何证据，只说各自的感受。Their comments were purely subjective, based on taste rather than on any standard.
sceneCN: 这里 subjective 是「主观的、凭个人感受的」（第 2 个义项：判断取决于感受而非证据）；句意：他们的评语完全是主观的，依据的是品味而不是任何标准。画面里可辨认的东西：两份评语、同一份草案、两种表情。

pos.zh: 主观的；主观性的；受个人情感或看法影响的
（语法）主格的；以主语形式出现的
（语法）主格形式；主语格

derivatives.zh: 由主观形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「主观地、凭个人感受地」
由主观形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「主观性、主观感受」
基础词，源自拉丁语 subjectum，义为「主体；主题；易受影响的」
由主观形容词加表示学说的名词词尾构成，义为「主观主义」
源出同一套拉丁语素，以「对象」为词根，义为「客观性」，与本词构成反义对

senses.title: Existing in the mind of the one who perceives
senses.titleCN: 只存在于感知者心中的
senses.definition: describing what belongs to a perceiving mind rather than to the thing outside it
senses.definitionCN: 描述只属于感知者的心智、而不属于外在之物的东西
senses.example: Colors are in one sense subjective, since they exist only for a seeing mind.
senses.exampleCN: 从某种意义上说，颜色是主观的，因为它们只为看见它们的心智而存在。
senses.why: The word begins in philosophy, where the subjectum is the bearer of thought, and whatever is real only for the bearer is called subjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起源于哲学，subjectum 指思想的承担者；凡是只为承担者而存在的东西，就被叫作主观的。

senses.title: Judged by personal feeling rather than evidence
senses.titleCN: 凭个人感受而非证据来判断
senses.definition: based on feelings, tastes or opinions that cannot be checked by anyone else
senses.definitionCN: 依据别人无法核对的感受、品味或意见
senses.example: Whether a soup is spicy enough is a subjective judgment.
senses.exampleCN: 一锅汤够不够辣，是一个主观判断。
senses.why: Once the philosophical sense met everyday judgment, the word began to label opinions that only the speaker can verify from the inside.
senses.whyCN: 哲学上的「只属于感知者」一旦进入日常判断，这个词就开始指那种只有说话者本人才能从内心里核对的意见。

senses.title: Expressing a personal point of view
senses.definition: said of writing or speech that shows the outlook of one person instead of claiming neutral description
senses.definitionCN: 形容写作或言谈展现某一个人的视角，而非声称中立描述
senses.example: The diary is subjective in tone, but it records exact times and prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这本日记在语气上是主观的，却记录了准确的时间与价格。
senses.why: A viewpoint can be declared rather than hidden; in this sense subjective is descriptive, not always a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 视角可以被明白说出，而不必藏着；这个义项里 subjective 是描述性的，并不总是贬义。

senses.title: The inner side of experience
senses.definition: the felt or experienced aspect of something, as opposed to what can be observed from outside
senses.definitionCN: 某事物被感受到、被经历的一面，相对于可从外部观察的一面
senses.example: Pain has a subjective side that no scan can measure.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛有一个扫描无法测量的主观层面。
senses.why: Two descriptions of one event can both be true: the temperature reading and the feeling of the cold.
senses.whyCN: 对同一件事的两种描述可以都成立：温度计的读数，与那个人觉得冷的感觉。

senses.title: Influenced by bias or partiality
senses.definition: distorted by interest, loyalty or prior belief, especially when presented as neutral
senses.definitionCN: 因利益、忠诚或原有信念而失真的，尤指却被当作中立呈现时
senses.example: A report written by the company itself is necessarily subjective.
senses.exampleCN: 由公司自己撰写的报告必然是主观的。
senses.why: The same word that names a personal view also names the risk of that view being passed off as fact, so it becomes a charge.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既指个人视角，也指这种视角被冒充为事实的风险，于是它成了一种指责。

senses.title: The grammatical subject case
senses.definition: denoting the case of a pronoun that forms the subject of a verb, such as I and he
senses.definitionCN: 指充当动词主语的代词所处的格，如 I 与 he
senses.example: English keeps the subjective case for pronouns such as I and we.
senses.exampleCN: 英语为 I、we 这类代词保留了主格形式。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the philosophical names too: what acts in a sentence is the subject, so its form is the subjective case.
senses.whyCN: 语法也借用了哲学的命名：在句子中行动的是主语，所以它的形式就叫主格。

senses.title: Taking place inside the patient
senses.definition: in medicine, describing a symptom that the patient feels rather than one a doctor can detect
senses.definitionCN: 医学上形容症状由病人自己感到，而非医生能够检查出来
senses.example: Fatigue is a subjective symptom, and it still matters.
senses.exampleCN: 疲乏是一种主观症状，可它依然重要。
senses.why: A symptom that lives only in what the patient says repeats the oldest idea: something is real to the one who holds it.
senses.whyCN: 只存在于病人口述中的症状，重复了最古老的想法：某物对持有它的人而言是真实的。

intro.en: Subjective is a learned adjective made in English from the Latin noun subjectum, something placed under. It was first used as a philosophical term, opposed to objective, and only later entered everyday judgment. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subjective 是在英语中由拉丁语名词 subjectum「被置于下方之物」构成的学术形容词。它起初是哲学术语，与 objective 相对，后来才进入日常判断。年代为约数。

items.en: Sub preceded by the prefix sub- means under, and iacere means to throw; subicere therefore meant to throw under or to subject.
items.cn: 动词 subicere 由前缀 sub-「在下」与 iacere「抛」构成，意为抛到下面，或使服从。

items.en: The past participle subjectum named what was placed beneath, and in Scholastic Latin it came to mean the bearer of attributes, the mind that holds properties.
items.cn: 过去分词 subjectum 指被置于下方之物；在中世纪经院拉丁语里，它转指属性的承担者，即持有属性的心智。

items.en: Scholars writing in Latin used subjectivus for whatever had its being in the subject, as opposed to objectivus, whatever had its being in the object.
items.cn: 用拉丁语写作的学者用 subjectivus 指存在于主体之中的东西，与 objectivus「存在于对象之中的」相对。

items.en: English writers adopted both words in the early seventeenth century; the pair carried into English exactly the philosophical opposition they had in Latin.
items.cn: 十七世纪初，英语作者同时借入了这两个词；这对词把拉丁语中的哲学对立原样带进了英语。

items.en: Philosophy split the pair: subjective described inner experience, objective described facts open to check, and the everyday sense in due course became a charge rather than a description.
items.cn: 哲学把这把词一分两半：subjective 描述内在经验，objective 描述可供核对的事实；后来日常语义逐渐变成一种指责，而不只是描述。

note.en: Group one collects words built on the same Latin base, and it also notices the modern verb that merely looks related; group two collects words for opinion, bias and the neutral thing they are measured against.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁词根构成的词，并点出现代动词只是形近；第二组收表示意见、偏见以及据以衡量的中立之物的词。

entries.definition: The matching adjective built from the same Latin family but on the object side; it describes what can be checked by anyone, so it is the direct opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 同一拉丁词族从「对象」一侧构成的配对形容词；它描述任何人可核对的东西，因此正好相反。

entries.definition: The abstract noun of this adjective: the quality or condition of being subjective, used especially in research and philosophy.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词的抽象名词：主观、主观性的性质或状态，尤用于研究与哲学。

entries.definition: The adverb: in a way shaped by personal feeling. It tells you how a judgment is made, while subjective describes the judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 相应的副词：以受个人感受影响的方式。它说明判断怎样作出，而 subjective 描述判断本身。

entries.definition: To bring a people under control. It shares the Latin pieces sub- and the yoke word iugum but not the throw word iacere, so it is only spelling-close to this family.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个民族受其控制。它共用拉丁语素 sub- 与表示「轭」的 iugum，却不含表示「抛」的 iacere，因此与本词族只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Leaning to one side by interest; it is almost always a criticism, while subjective can simply name where an experience lives.
entries.definitionCN: 因利益而偏向一边；它几乎总是贬义，而 subjective 可以只是指出经验所在的层面。

entries.definition: Belonging to one person and not shared; it says whose it is, without saying whether it can be checked.
entries.definitionCN: 属于一个人而不与他人共享；它只说明归谁所有，不评价能否核对。

entries.definition: Openly committed to one party or cause; unlike subjective, it does not hide behind a claim of neutrality.
entries.definitionCN: 公开站在某一派或某个事业一边；与 subjective 不同，它不躲在「中立」的说法后面。

entries.definition: The standard against which subjective judgment is complained about: facts that others can check for themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 主观判断被抱怨时拿来对照的标准：别人可以亲自核对的事实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin base, the real opposite pair and the real everyday collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依靠真实的拉丁词根、真实的反义配对与真实的日常搭配。

normal.en: Subject plus -ive: whatever belongs to the subject who perceives is subjective.
normal.cn: subject 加形容词词尾 -ive：凡属于那个感知的主体的，就是主观的。

normal.en: Subjective and objective are a matched pair, so learning one shows you the other.
normal.cn: subjective 与 objective 是一对配套词，学一个就等于学了另一个。

normal.en: A subjective judgment starts with the person; an objective finding starts with the evidence.
normal.cn: 主观判断从人出发；客观发现从证据出发。

normal.en: The adverb is subjectively and the noun is subjectivity; the endings keep the same stress pattern.
normal.cn: 副词是 subjectively，名词是 subjectivity；这几个词尾保持了相近的重音走向。

normal.en: In grammar the subjective case is the case of the subject, as in he, not him.
normal.cn: 语法里 the subjective case 就是主格，例如 he 而不用 him。

abstract.en: Picture two people in front of one painting, one warmed and one chilled.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人站在同一幅画前，一个觉得暖，一个觉得冷。

abstract.en: Think of tinted glasses: the road is the same, the colour you see is yours.
abstract.cn: 想想有色眼镜：道路是同一段，看到的颜色却是你的。

abstract.en: Picture a reviewer writing one word in the margin, a word nobody else can check.
abstract.cn: 想象评审在页边写下一个词，那是一个别人无法核对的词。

examples.en: Taste in poetry is highly subjective and varies from reader to reader.
examples.cn: 对诗歌的品味高度主观，因人而异。

examples.en: The survey asked respondents to rate their subjective sense of wellbeing.
examples.cn: 这项调查请受访者给自己的主观幸福感打分。

examples.en: In formal English the pronoun after the verb be stays in the subjective case.
examples.cn: 在正式英语中，动词 be 之后的代词仍用主格形式。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 在下 + ject 抛」——被放在心底下、由自己承担的那一面，就是主观的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 subjectum（被置于下方之物，上溯 subicere「抛在下、使服从」，由 sub-「在下」与 iacere「抛」构成）+ 形容词词尾 -ive；核心义是「属于感知者的」，与 objectivus「属于对象的」相对，17 世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses start where the word began, in a mind that holds something only for itself, then move to judgment, viewpoint, inner experience, bias, the grammatical subject case and the medical symptom.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项从词源处开始：某物只为一颗心智而存在；随后走向凭感受作判断、表达个人视角、经验的内在一面、偏见、语法主格，最后是医学上的主观症状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people before one painting, each carrying away a different warmth while the frame stays still.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人站在同一幅画前，各自带走不同的温度，画框纹丝不动。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: what exists only for the perceiving mind.
branches.cn: 源头：只为感知者的心智而存在的东西。

branches.en: JUDGMENT AND VOICE: a verdict built on feeling, and a text built on one point of view.
branches.cn: 判断与声音：凭感受得出的结论，与从单一视角写成的文本。

branches.en: THE INNER SIDE: experience felt from within, including symptoms only the patient can report.
branches.cn: 内在之面：从内部被感受到的经验，包括只有病人才能报告的症状。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: the same word turns into an accusation when feeling is passed off as fact.
branches.cn: 指责：当感受被冒充为事实，同一个词就变成了指控。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the philosophical subject becomes the actor in a sentence, so its form is the subject case.
branches.cn: 语法：哲学上的主体成为句中的行动者，于是它的形式叫主格。

intro.en: Subjective is built on the Latin stem subject- plus the adjective ending -ive, and the prefix sub- is the same one that makes submarine and submit.
intro.cn: subjective 建立在拉丁词干 subject- 与形容词词尾 -ive 之上，其中的前缀 sub- 与 submarine、submit 里的是同一个。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from subicere and subiectivus through subject and subjective to the English pair objective and objectivity.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 subicere 与 subiectivus 一路走到 subject、subjective，再走到英语中配对的 objective 与 objectivity。

items.example: Sub- places a thing lower, as in submarine and subsoil.
items.exampleCN: sub- 把事物放到更低处，如 submarine 与 subsoil。

items.example: Iacere lies behind the ject of reject and project.
items.exampleCN: iacere 是 reject 与 project 中 ject 的来源。

items.example: Subicere is the verb behind subjectum.
items.exampleCN: subicere 是 subjectum 背后的动词。

items.example: Subiectivus was used in learned Latin from the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: subiectivus 自十六世纪起用于学术拉丁语。

items.meaningCN: 主体；主题；受试者；易受影响的
items.example: Subject is the base from which subjective grows.
items.exampleCN: subject 是主观形容词赖以生长的基词。

items.example: The ending -ive turns subject into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 把 subject 变成形容词。

items.example: Subjective judgment starts with the person.
items.exampleCN: 主观判断从人出发。

items.example: The ending -ly makes subjectively.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 subjectively。

items.example: The ending -ity makes subjectivity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 subjectivity。

items.example: The prefix ob- gives objective and objection.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ob- 构成 objective 与 objection。

latinEntries.meaning: what is placed under; the subject

definition_zh: 阈下的；潜意识里的；未达到意识水平的
definition_en: too faint or too brief to be noticed consciously, yet still able to affect the mind
core_image: 电影画面一帧里掠过一句爆米花广告，快到没人看见，散场时却有人去买
scene: 银幕上闪过一帧提示，时长太短，观众都说没注意到，可散场后许多人走的方向出奇一致。The message was so brief that it stayed subliminal, yet some viewers still changed their minds.
sceneCN: 这里 subliminal 是「阈下的、未达到意识水平的」（第 1 个义项：低于感知阈限）；句意：那条信息短到一直停在阈下，可仍有观众改变了主意。画面里可辨认的东西：一帧闪过的画面、一排座椅、散场的人流、一桶爆米花。

pos.zh: 阈下的；潜意识里的；未达到意识水平的

derivatives.zh: 由阈下形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「以阈下的方式、在意识之下地」
拉丁语表示「门槛」的名词，心理学借来表示「阈限」，是本词的第二部分
由 limen 加形容词词尾构成，义为「阈限的、处于过渡边缘的」
把前缀 sub- 换成表示「在上」的 supra-，义为「阈上的、足以被察觉的」，与本词相反
本土词，义为「门槛；阈限」，常在需要用英文解释 limen 时替代它

senses.title: Below the threshold of sensation
senses.definition: said of a stimulus that is too weak, too faint or too brief to produce a reportable sensation
senses.definitionCN: 形容刺激太弱、太淡或太短，因而无法产生可报告的感知
senses.example: A sound twelve decibels below the touch threshold remains subliminal.
senses.exampleCN: 比可听阈限低十二分贝的声音仍属阈下。
senses.why: The Latin second half of the word means threshold, so anything under the threshold is under the line where sensing begins.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁语后半部分意为「门槛」，所以凡在门槛之下的东西，就在「能够感知」这条线以下。

senses.title: Outside conscious awareness
senses.definition: influencing thought or feeling without the person being aware of the influence at the time
senses.definitionCN: 在本人当时并不察觉的情况下影响其思想或感受
senses.example: The choice was shaped by a subliminal stereotype.
senses.exampleCN: 这个选择受到一种阈下刻板印象的影响。
senses.why: Once the threshold is understood as the line of awareness rather than of the senses, anything under the line goes unnoticed but still works.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把门槛理解为「觉察」的那条线而非感官的线，线下的东西就会在不被注意时仍然起作用。

senses.title: Hidden messages in advertising
senses.definition: a message flashed or embedded so briefly that the viewer cannot consciously read it, claimed to sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 闪现或嵌入得极短、观众无法有意识地读出的信息，被声称可以推销商品
senses.example: The pop-corn subliminal story was told so often that many people accepted it as fact.
senses.exampleCN: 关于爆米花的阈下广告传闻被讲得太多次，以至于许多人把它当成了事实。
senses.why: In the middle of the century the word escaped the laboratory and became a claim about power over the wallet, which is how it is best remembered.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪中期，这个词走出实验室，变成一种「能左右钱包」的说法，这也是它最容易被记住的一面。

senses.title: The faint effect of hidden cues
senses.titleCN: 隐蔽提示带来的微弱影响
senses.definition: a small, short-lived shift in judgment after a cue that was masked, ignored or unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 在被遮蔽、被忽略或未被注意的提示之后出现的短暂而小幅的判断变化
senses.example: Laboratory studies find only weak and short-lived subliminal effects.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室研究只发现微弱而短暂的阈下效应。
senses.why: Modern experiments keep the threshold but lower the ambition: under-line messages can nudge a rating, not take over a mind.
senses.whyCN: 现代实验保留了「门槛」这个概念，却把期望调低：线下的信息能轻轻推动评分，却接管不了一颗心。

senses.title: A hint too subtle to name
senses.titleCN: 细微到说不出名字的暗示
senses.definition: an ordinary hint, tone or detail so slight that the person calls it intuition rather than sensing it
senses.definitionCN: 极细微的语气、暗示或细节，细微到本人称之为直觉，而非感到自己在感知
senses.example: Her unease was subliminal, a shade of tone she could not name.
senses.exampleCN: 她的不安是阈下的，是一种她说不出名字的语气。
senses.why: The word stretched from stimulus to feelings, so everyday speech now uses it for knowledge that has no traceable source.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从刺激扩展到感受，于是日常说法用它来形容那种说不出来源的知识。

senses.title: Below the level of importance
senses.titleCN: 分量不到、不值得在意的
senses.definition: in looser writing, so slight as to be practically negligible, sometimes in an ironic or playful tone
senses.definitionCN: 在较宽松的写作中，表示细微到几乎可以忽略，有时带反讽或玩笑语气
senses.example: The criticism was subliminal, not even worth a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 那点批评是阈下的，连回一句都不值得。
senses.why: The threshold is also the line between worth noticing and not worth noticing, so the word drifts into a verdict on trifles.
senses.whyCN: 门槛也分开了「值得注意」与「不值得注意」，于是这个词慢慢变成了对琐碎之事的评判。

senses.title: The borderline case
senses.definition: a brief, partial or borderline residue of perception that the person cannot quite report
senses.definitionCN: 短暂、不完整或处于边界的感知残留，本人难以准确报告
senses.example: A word spoken just at the subliminal boundary may be half heard.
senses.exampleCN: 恰好在阈下边界说出的话可能只被听到一半。
senses.why: The threshold is a line, and lines have edges, where the under and the over touch and the answer is uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 门槛是一条线，线有边缘；在边缘处，「阈下」与「阈上」相接，答案也变得不确定。

intro.en: Subliminal is a nineteenth-century learned compound: Latin sub-, under, joined to limen, threshold. It was made for psychology, not inherited whole from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: subliminal 是十九世纪按拉丁语素造出的学术复合词：拉丁前缀 sub-「在下」加名词 limen「门槛」。它是为心理学而造的，并非整词沿袭拉丁语。年代为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant under or below and was attached freely to Latin stems, as in subicere, to throw under, and sublevare, to lift up.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，在拉丁语词干前可自由附着，如 subicere「抛在下」、sublevare「托起」。

items.en: Limen meant threshold, the sill of a door, and it also named the first point at which something begins.
items.cn: limen 意为门槛、门下的横木，也指某事物开始的第一点。

items.en: Psychophysicists measured the limen as the point where a stimulus becomes just noticeable, and the Latin noun became their technical term for it.
items.cn: 心理物理学家把 limen 测量为刺激刚刚可察觉的那一点，这个拉丁名词于是成了此项测量的技术术语。

items.en: Writers on the new psychology built subliminal by putting sub- before limen, to name what lies under that measured line of awareness.
items.cn: 新心理学的作者们把 sub- 加在 limen 之前，造出 subliminal，用来指处于那条被测量出的觉察线之下的东西。

items.en: Popular accounts of hidden advertising in the 1950s carried the laboratory word into the newspapers, where it named a claim about hidden power rather than a measured effect.
items.cn: 二十世纪五十年代关于隐蔽广告的通俗报道，把这个实验室用词带进了报纸；在那里，它指的是一种关于隐蔽力量的说法，而不是被测量出的效应。

note.en: Group one holds the neighbours built on the Latin word for threshold, together with the look-alike formed on a different Latin word; group two holds words for what happens outside full awareness.
note.cn: 第一组收由拉丁语「门槛」一词构成的邻近词，以及来自另一个拉丁词的形近词；第二组收表示「在完全觉察之外发生之事」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective from limen without a prefix: it describes what is at the threshold or in a transitional stage, as in rites of passage.
entries.definitionCN: 不带前缀的同一词根的形容词：描述处于门槛上或过渡阶段的东西，如过渡仪式。

entries.definition: The Latin noun itself: the threshold or the smallest stimulus that can be sensed.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁名词本身：门槛，或能引起感觉的最小刺激。

entries.definition: The same word with a prefix meaning above, so it describes any stimulus strong enough to be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 同形结构换成表示「在上」的前缀，因此指强到能被注意到的刺激。

entries.definition: Describing an impulse turned into something higher, or a solid turned straight into vapour. It comes from sublimis, raised up, not from limen; it is only spelling-close to this word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容冲动被升华为更高之物，或固体直接化为气体。它来自 sublimis「高处的」，与 limen 无关；与本词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Said of mental activity or of a person who is not aware; it covers states of much greater hiddenness than the slim margin under the threshold.
entries.definitionCN: 形容意识不到的心理活动或人；它涵盖的隐藏程度远大于门槛下那窄窄的一条。

entries.definition: Too slight to be perceived at all. Subliminal means under the perceiving line yet still acting; imperceptible usually just means nothing is there to feel.
entries.definitionCN: 细微到任何感知都无从发生。subliminal 指感知线之下却仍在起作用；imperceptible 通常只是说没有什么可感觉的东西。

entries.definition: Present but not spelled out, such as an implicit rule; it says nothing about whether the person can notice it.
entries.definitionCN: 存在却未被明说，如隐含的规则；它不涉及本人能否注意到。

entries.definition: Simply not noticed, by anyone, for any reason; the word makes no claim about sensory thresholds.
entries.definitionCN: 只是没被注意到，不论是谁、出于什么原因；这个词完全不涉及感觉阈限。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real technical family and the real laboratory findings.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依靠真实的拉丁语素、真实的技术词族与真实的实验结果。

normal.en: Limen is threshold, so subliminal means under the threshold, and liminal alone means at it.
normal.cn: limen 是门槛，所以 subliminal 意为「门槛之下」，单用 liminal 则是「就在门槛上」。

normal.en: The opposite is formed with a prefix meaning above, which gives supraliminal.
normal.cn: 反义形式用表示「在上」的前缀构成，也就是 supraliminal。

normal.en: In psychology the limen is measured as the just noticeable difference, and subliminal stimuli fall just short of it.
normal.cn: 心理学把 limen 测量为刚刚能察觉的差异，而阈下刺激恰好差一点达不到它。

normal.en: One word hides the prefix and one hides the threshold: sub is under, limen is the line.
normal.cn: 这个词里藏着一个前缀和一个门槛：sub 是「在下」，limen 是那条线。

normal.en: Medical and eye clinics use the word for pressure under the limen of pain, which is the same under-the-line idea.
normal.cn: 医学与眼科把这个词用于「疼痛阈下」的压力，仍是同一个「线下」的思路。

abstract.en: Picture a word flashed on a screen for one frame, gone before the eye can read it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个字在银幕上只亮了一帧，眼睛还没读完它就消失了。

abstract.en: Picture a doorman who lets in nothing that he can clearly see, yet the hall still fills.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门房，凡他看清的东西都不放进来，可大厅却渐渐坐满了人。

abstract.en: Sounds like sub plus liminal: sit just below the line that marks the start of noticing.
abstract.cn: 读作 sub 加 liminal：正好坐在「开始注意到」那条线之下。

examples.en: The subliminal image appeared for a single frame and left no trace in memory.
examples.cn: 那幅阈下图像出现的频率不到每秒一帧。

examples.en: Critics argued that subliminal advertising could not make anyone buy anything.
examples.cn: 批评者认为阈下广告无法让人去买任何东西。

examples.en: Participants showed a small shift in rating after a subliminally presented face.
examples.cn: 在阈下呈现一张面孔之后，参与者的评分出现了小幅变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 在下 + limen 门槛」——声音或画面还没跨过「能被察觉」那道门槛，就被叫作阈下的；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ limen（门槛），意指心理物理学的「阈限」（limen）之下的刺激，即感觉不到却仍起作用者；此词为十九世纪末心理学按拉丁语素新造，非古典拉丁词。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses run from the laboratory line of sensation, through awareness and the famous advertising claim, to tiny measured effects, unnameable hints, negligible trifles and finally the boundary itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项从实验室里的感觉阈限出发，经觉察线、著名的广告传闻、被测量出的微小效应、说不出名字的暗示、可忽略的琐事，最后回到边界本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one frame of a message passing on the screen too quickly for the eye to read, yet not too quickly for the mind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一帧信息在银幕上飞过，眼睛来不及读，心智却未必来不及。

branches.en: THE LINE: a stimulus under the measured threshold, and the uncertain margin right at it.
branches.cn: 那条线：阈值之下的刺激，以及恰好压在线上、答案不明的那一带。

branches.en: THE INNER WORKING: an influence not noticed, and a hint too slight to be given a name.
branches.cn: 内部运作：未被注意的影响，与细微到叫不出名字的暗示。

branches.en: THE CLAIM: hidden messages in advertising, a story bigger than the evidence.
branches.cn: 那个说法：广告里的隐蔽信息，故事远远大于证据。

branches.en: THE MEASUREMENT: small, short effects found only under careful controls.
branches.cn: 测量：只有在严格控制下才能发现的小幅、短暂效应。

branches.en: THE TRIFLE: the threshold as the line between worth noticing and not.
branches.cn: 琐事：门槛被读成「值不值得留意」的分界。

intro.en: Subliminal is the Latin prefix sub- plus limen, threshold, and the image of a line below which nothing is quite noticed runs through the whole family.
intro.cn: subliminal 由拉丁前缀 sub- 与 limen「门槛」构成，而「在一条线之下，什么都不太被注意到」这一意象贯穿整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gave both halves: sub- is the ordinary prefix for under, and limen is the ordinary noun for a threshold, which psychology turned into a measurable limit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了两个成分：sub- 是表示「在下」的常用前缀，limen 是表示「门槛」的常用名词；心理学把它变成可测量的界限。

items.example: Sub- appears in submarine, subsoil and suborder.
items.exampleCN: sub- 出现在 submarine、subsoil 与 suborder 中。

items.example: Limen gives the second half of subliminal.
items.exampleCN: limen 提供 subliminal 的后半部分。

items.example: The ending -al turns a noun stem into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把名词词干变成形容词。

items.example: A subliminal sound lies below the hearing limit.
items.exampleCN: 阈下的声音处于听觉限度之下。

items.example: The ending -ly gives subliminally.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 subliminally。

items.example: Liminal marks a transition rather than a hidden layer.
items.exampleCN: liminal 标记过渡阶段，而不是隐藏的一层。

items.example: Supra- builds the opposite word supraliminal.
items.exampleCN: supra- 构成反义词 supraliminal。

items.example: Only supraliminal stimuli can be reported.
items.exampleCN: 只有阈上刺激才能被报告出来。

items.example: Threshold is how psychologists say limen in English.
items.exampleCN: threshold 是心理学家用英语说 limen 的方式。

definition_zh: 亚目（生物分类中介于目与科之间的等级）；次级的目；（修道）副会
definition_en: a rank in biological classification below an order and above a family, grouping together related families
core_image: 一株大树的枝杈上再分出小杈：主干是一次分枝，亚目是同一根大枝上的第二次分叉
scene: 标本馆里，一整排甲虫按体型与触角排成几个大柜，每一个大柜又分成若干小抽屉，标签上写着各自的名字。The beetles were divided into suborders that contained several families each.
sceneCN: 这里 suborder 指「亚目」（第 1 个义项：目的下一级分类阶元）；句意：这些甲虫被分进各自包含若干科的亚目里。画面里可辨认的东西：一排标本柜、若干小抽屉、大柜与小抽屉的标签、甲虫标本。

pos.zh: 亚目（生物分类中介于目与科之间的等级）
次级的目；次级组织或分类
（修道会）副会；次级修会

derivatives.zh: 由亚目名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「亚目级的、属于亚目的」
基础词，源自拉丁语 ordo，义为「次序；等级；目」
同一拉丁语素堆叠构成，义为「次要的；下级；使从属」
由从属形容词加名词词尾构成，义为「隶属、从属关系」，与亚目同属「放在下一级」的思路
由拉丁语 ordo 加形容词词尾构成，义为「序数的；按次序排列的」

senses.title: The rank between order and family
senses.titleCN: 位于目与科之间的分类等级
senses.definition: a taxonomic rank below an order that groups several related families together
senses.definitionCN: 位于目之下的分类等级，用来把若干近缘的科归在一起
senses.example: Kangaroos belong to the marsupial order, which is split into several suborders.
senses.exampleCN: 袋鼠属于有袋类这个目，而这个目被分为若干亚目。
senses.why: Latin sub- means under and order comes from Latin ordo, a row or rank, so a suborder is literally the row that sits just beneath one order.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁前缀 sub- 意为「在下」，order 来自拉丁语 ordo「一排、一等级」，所以亚目就是紧挨着某个目、排在它下一行的那个等级。

senses.title: The name of a group at that rank
senses.titleCN: 处于该等级的类群名称
senses.definition: the group of animals or plants that a scientist places at that rank, and the word that names it
senses.definitionCN: 科学家放在这一等级上的一群动物或植物，以及命名它们的那个词
senses.example: In birds the suborder is written after the order and before the family.
senses.exampleCN: 在鸟类分类中，亚目写在目之后、科之前。
senses.why: A rank is a place in a ladder, while a suborder in use also means the group that lives at that place, so the word names both the rung and its occupants.
senses.whyCN: 等级是梯子上的一格，而实际使用的亚目也指住在这格里的那一群，因此这个词既指那一格，也指格中的东西。

senses.title: The one that holds the order-naming group
senses.titleCN: 收有原命名的类的亚目
senses.definition: the suborder that contains the family which gave the whole order its name
senses.definitionCN: 含有那个为整个目命名的科的亚目
senses.example: The type suborder keeps the original name of the order.
senses.exampleCN: 模式亚目沿用原来的目名。
senses.why: Each split creates a family that was named first, and the suborder holding it becomes the anchor against which the rest are measured.
senses.whyCN: 每次拆分都会留下一个最早命名的科，收着它的亚目就成了锚点，其他亚目以此对照。

senses.title: A required step in some codes
senses.titleCN: 某些命名法规要求的一级
senses.definition: a rank that certain codes insist must be recognised before some families can be grouped
senses.definitionCN: 某些命名法规坚持必须先确立的等级，某些科才可以据此归并
senses.example: Under the naming code the suborder is not optional for that group.
senses.exampleCN: 按照命名法规，那一类群不能省掉亚目这一级。
senses.why: Names do not sort themselves: a code has to decide which rungs a classification may use and which it must use.
senses.whyCN: 名称不会自己排好，总得有法规决定，一部分类体系可以用哪些格子，又必须用哪些格子。

senses.title: A secondary order
senses.definition: in general speech, a lesser or secondary ordering or ranking, not restricted to biology
senses.definitionCN: 在日常说法中，指次要的一档排序或等级，不限于生物学
senses.example: Within this suborder of questions, the easiest ones come first.
senses.exampleCN: 在这类次级的问题里，最容易的排在前面。
senses.why: Since order has long meant arrangement in general, a suborder in ordinary writing is simply any arrangement tucked inside a larger one.
senses.whyCN: order 长久以来也泛指排列，所以在日常写作里，亚目式的说法就只是指嵌在更大排列里的那一层排列。

senses.title: The plural name for the whole group
senses.definition: a name-like plural used for a broad group of related organisms, usually ending in a set suffix
senses.definitionCN: 以固定词尾表示一大群近缘生物的类群式复数名称
senses.example: The plural form often appears as a taxonomic name with a fixed ending.
senses.exampleCN: 复数形式常以固定词尾出现，作为一个分类学名称。
senses.why: Nomenclature usually wants a single name per group, so the habit of writing the plural instead is informal and best avoided in formal work.
senses.whyCN: 命名实践通常要求每个类群只用一个名称，所以把复数当类群名的写法不正式，在正式写作里最好避免。

senses.title: The monastic sub-order
senses.definition: a secondary branch of a religious order, such as a group of converts attached to an older monastery
senses.definitionCN: 宗教修会的次级分支，例如附属于旧日修道院的归化者团体
senses.example: The medieval suborder cared for the sick while the main house prayed.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪的副会负责照料病人，而主院负责祈祷。
senses.why: The word order also means a religious order, so sub-. plus that sense gives any smaller branch of a religious body.
senses.whyCN: order 也指修道会，所以把「在下」的前缀加上这一义项，就得到了宗教团体中的分支。

intro.en: Suborder is a scientific compound of two Latin units, the prefix sub- and ordo, a row or rank. The biological use belongs to modern classification, while the use for a branch of a monastic order is older. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: suborder 是由两个拉丁成分构成的科学复合词：前缀 sub- 与 ordo「一排、等级」。生物学义属于近代分类学；而指修道会分支的用法更早。年代为约数。

items.en: Sub- meant under or below and was already used in Latin to rank one thing beneath another, as in submit.
items.cn: sub- 意为「在下、低于」，拉丁语中已用它把一物排在另一物之下，如 submit。

items.en: Ordo meant a row, a line or an established rank, and it named social classes as well as arranged lines.
items.cn: ordo 意为行列、队伍或既定的等级，既指排好的行列，也指社会阶层。

items.en: Through French, ordo reached English as order and spread quickly from arrangement to command, from ranking to religious community.
items.cn: ordo 经法语以 order 的形式进入英语，并迅速从「排列」扩展到「命令」，从「等级」扩展到「宗教团体」。

items.en: The word for a lesser branch of a religious community is the oldest recorded use of suborder, and it is now rare.
items.cn: 指宗教团体次级分支的用法是本词最早见于记录的义项，如今已很少使用。

items.en: Biological classification adopted the same pieces for the rank under an order; the name works like a shelf label under the main shelf.
items.cn: 生物分类学用同样的成分造出「目之下一级」的名称；这个词就像主书架下方的小标签。

note.en: Group one collects the piece built from order, with the look-alikes from ordo, each from a slightly different stem, along with one near neighbour; group two collects the classification ranks that sit above, below and beside this one.
note.cn: 第一组收由 order 构成的词，以及同样出自拉丁语 ordo 的形近词与近邻词；第二组收位于本词上一级、下一级与同一层的分类阶元。

entries.definition: The base noun: arrangement, command, or in biology the rank one step above a suborder.
entries.definitionCN: 基础名词：排列、命令，或生物学中比亚目高一级的阶元。

entries.definition: Built on the same ordo but from a different stem: it describes numbers that show position, as in first and second.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 ordo 但词干不同：形容表示位置的数词，如 first、second。

entries.definition: Latin sub- plus ordo again, but meaning placed in a lower rank or made to serve; it is about people and things, not taxonomy.
entries.definitionCN: 仍是拉丁 sub- 加 ordo，但意为「被排在较低等级或使人听命」；讲的是人和事物，而不是分类学。

entries.definition: An outlying district of a city. It shares sub- but is built on urbs, the city, not ordo, so it is only spelling-close to this word.
entries.definitionCN: 城市的边缘区。它共用 sub-，却建立在 urbs「城市」之上而非 ordo 之上，因此与本词只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A place in an ordered series; suborder is one particular rung in the taxonomic ladder rather than the idea of a rung.
entries.definitionCN: 有序系列中的一个位置；suborder 是分类梯子上某一格的具体名称，而不是「梯格」这个一般概念。

entries.definition: The rank sitting directly under a suborder; families are grouped into suborders, which are grouped into orders.
entries.definitionCN: 紧接在亚目之下的阶元；科归入亚目，亚目再归入目。

entries.definition: A rank inserted between suborder and family when the grouping is crowded, which shows that ranks are tools rather than fixed lengths.
entries.definitionCN: 当类群太拥挤时插在亚目与科之间的阶元，说明等级是可以调整的工具，而非固定长度。

entries.definition: In botany, an informal category below family; it names a division of a group without claiming a fixed rank.
entries.definitionCN: 植物学中低于科的非正式类别；它只表示某个类群中的划分，不声称有固定等级。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin pieces, the real ladder of ranks and the real uses in biology and religion.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想依靠真实的拉丁语素、真实的阶元阶梯，以及生物学与宗教中的真实用法。

normal.en: Sub means under and order is a rank, so a suborder is simply the rank under an order.
normal.cn: sub 是「在下」，order 是一级，所以 suborder 就是目之下的那一级。

normal.en: The ladder runs order, suborder, family; the name tells you both ends it is squeezed between.
normal.cn: 阶梯是目、亚目、科；这个名字把被夹在中间的两端都说了出来。

normal.en: The adjective is subordinal, built with the same ending as ordinal, which itself comes from order.
normal.cn: 形容词是 subordinal，用的是与 ordinal 相同的词尾，而 ordinal 也来自 order。

normal.en: Subordinate uses the same sub plus order pieces but means a person or thing placed lower, not a taxonomic rung.
normal.cn: subordinate 用的是同样的 sub 加 order 成分，但指被排在较低位置的人或事，而不是分类阶元。

normal.en: Because order also means an order of monks, a suborder can name its lesser branch.
normal.cn: 由于 order 也指修道会，suborder 也可以指其中的次级分支。

abstract.en: Picture a large cabinet of specimens divided into drawers, and each drawer divided again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个大标本柜先分成若干抽屉，每个抽屉又再分开。

abstract.en: Picture a tree branch that forks twice: the first fork is the order, the second is the suborder.
abstract.cn: 想象一根树枝分了两次杈：第一次分杈是目，第二次分杈是亚目。

abstract.en: Sounds like sub plus order: a shelf hung just below the main shelf.
abstract.cn: 读作 sub 加 order：一排行货架挂在主货架的正下方。

examples.en: Beetles are divided into four suborders, one of which contains most species.
examples.cn: 甲虫被分为四个亚目，其中一个包含了大多数物种。

examples.en: The suborder contains four families and about two hundred species.
examples.cn: 这个亚目包含四个科，约两百个物种。

examples.en: Some zoologists place the group in a suborder of its own.
examples.cn: 有些动物学家把这个类群单独立为一个亚目。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「sub 在下 + order 目」——目下面那一级，就是亚目；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub-（在下）+ ordo（行列、等级，英语 order）——置于某一「目」之下的一级；生物分类中的亚目，亦用于宗教团体的次级分支。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses run from the rank itself, through the group that occupies it, the type suborder and the naming rules, to the looser idea of a secondary order and the older, rarer use for a religious branch.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项从等级本身出发，经占用这一等级的类群、模式亚目与命名规则，再到「次级排列」这一宽松说法，最后是较古老、如今少见的宗教分支义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch that forks a second time, hanging just below its parent branch.
core.cn: 核心意象：第二次分杈的枝条，就挂在母枝下方。

branches.en: THE RANK AND ITS OCCUPANTS: a rung between order and family, and the group that lives on it.
branches.cn: 等级与住户：目与科之间的一格，以及住在这格里的类群。

branches.en: THE ANCHOR: the suborder that keeps the old name, and the rules that require the rank.
branches.cn: 锚点与规则：沿用旧名的那个亚目，以及要求设立这一级的法规。

branches.en: THE LOOSE SENSE: any secondary ordering, once order is taken as arrangement in general.
branches.cn: 宽松义项：一旦把 order 理解为一般排列，任何次级排列都可称之。

branches.en: THE HABIT: writing the plural for the group, a usage formal work avoids.
branches.cn: 习惯：用复数指整个类群，正式写作应避免。

branches.en: THE OLD BRANCH: the mediaeval sense borrowed from the religious order.
branches.cn: 古老分支：借自修道会之「会」的用法。

intro.en: Suborder is the Latin prefix sub- joined to order, itself from Latin ordo, and the family of words descending from ordo shows the two ideas of row and command.
intro.cn: suborder 是拉丁前缀 sub- 加 order 构成，而 order 来自拉丁语 ordo；由 ordo 衍生的一族词把「行列」与「命令」两种意思都保存了下来。

latinIntro.en: Both pieces are Latin: sub- is the ordinary prefix for under, and ordo is the ordinary noun for a row, a line or an established rank.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都来自拉丁语：sub- 是表示「在下」的常用前缀，ordo 是表示行列、队伍或既定等级的常用名词。

items.example: Sub- builds submarine, subsoil and suborder.
items.exampleCN: sub- 构成 submarine、subsoil 与 suborder。

items.example: Ordo is the source of order and suborder.
items.exampleCN: ordo 是 order 与 suborder 的来源。

items.example: Order names the rank one step above a suborder.
items.exampleCN: order 指比亚目高一级的那个阶元。

items.example: The suborder groups four families together.
items.exampleCN: 该亚目把四个科归在一起。

items.example: A subordinal name records the rank.
items.exampleCN: 亚目名称记录了它所属的等级。

items.example: Ordinal shares the source of order.
items.exampleCN: ordinal 与 order 同源。

items.example: Subordinate uses the same two Latin pieces.
items.exampleCN: subordinate 使用了同样的两个拉丁成分。

items.example: The ending -al turns suborder into subordinal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 suborder 变成 subordinal。

items.example: Super- marks a rank above, as in superfamily.
items.exampleCN: super- 表示高于一级，如 superfamily。

latinEntries.meaning: to put in a lower rank
